name: Patty Murray
subject: The biggest blue wave midterm since 2006
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY PEOPLE FOR PATTY MURRAY
body:
History is watching – so I need every member of this grassroots team to step up.
| | |
---
Peter – I know your inbox is probably flooded with emails from political campaigns or advocacy organizations, including mine. I’m grateful that you’re even reading this right now.

**So out of respect for your time, I’ll get to the point:**

**We have just 4 days left of this campaign.**
John Sununu has taken the lead in the polls thanks to over $67 million in GOP spending -- and they're taking over the New Hampshire airwaves.
We're running out of time to close this critical gap and keep New Hampshire blue.
**[Will you chip in $10 or whatever you can afford today to boost our grassroots campaign and help flip the Senate?](https://substack.com/redirect/b88a1360-d833-4d6b-a32b-ec1a86992396?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ DONATE](https://substack.com/redirect/b88a1360-d833-4d6b-a32b-ec1a86992396?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**Karoline Leavitt and I go way back.**
Before she was standing behind the podium in Donald Trump's White House briefing room, Granite Staters got an up-close look at her style of politics when she ran against me for Congress here in New Hampshire in 2022.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b88a1360-d833-4d6b-a32b-ec1a86992396?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
[DONATE](https://substack.com/redirect/b88a1360-d833-4d6b-a32b-ec1a86992396?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The outrage. The constant performative attacks. The obsession with Donald Trump and the MAGA movement, instead of the issues Granite Staters were actually facing.
_And New Hampshire rejected her MAGA agenda._
Don't get me wrong: Granite Staters are fiercely independent. Voters split tickets, ask hard questions, and expect candidates to _earn_ their votes.
_But Granite Staters also have common sense._
While Karoline Leavitt was chasing cable news attention and auditioning to become a national MAGA celebrity, New Hampshire families were worried about housing costs, child care, grocery bills, and whether they could still afford to stay in the communities where they grew up.
**I 've always believed this job is about service, not stardom.** That means showing up, solving problems, and doing the work -- even when no one's paying attention.
And while that approach may not always generate headlines, it's how I've delivered real results: lowering prescription drug costs, protecting veterans' benefits, supporting small businesses, defending reproductive freedom, and standing up for Medicare and Social Security.
And it stands in stark contrast to the brand of politics Karoline Leavitt built her campaign around.
**Now the GOP is trying to bring that same MAGA playbook back to New Hampshire in this Senate race.**
They know this seat could decide control of the Senate. They know New Hampshire is one of the biggest battlegrounds in the country. And they're spending millions of dollars trying to flip this seat and install another reliable vote for Trump's agenda.
Because if the last few years have taught us anything, it's that the MAGA movement doesn't really care whether its politics fit New Hampshire. They'll still try to force them here anyway.
But here's what they still don't understand about our state:
People here want leaders who are grounded in their communities and focused on making life better for the people they represent.
That's what this campaign is about.
_Not the noise._
_Not the insults._
_Not trying to go viral by saying the most outrageous thing on TV._
**Granite Staters rejected Karoline Leavitt 's MAGA agenda when it was on the ballot here. They saw through the spin and chose a different path.**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b88a1360-d833-4d6b-a32b-ec1a86992396?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
[DONATE](https://substack.com/redirect/b88a1360-d833-4d6b-a32b-ec1a86992396?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Now we have to do it again -- because the stakes are even higher this time.
**[What happens in this race will shape the direction of New Hampshire for years to come. Chip in $15 or whatever you can right now to help us hold this critical open Senate seat and deliver for Granite Staters.](https://substack.com/redirect/b88a1360-d833-4d6b-a32b-ec1a86992396?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ DONATE](https://substack.com/redirect/b88a1360-d833-4d6b-a32b-ec1a86992396?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
We're talking about decisions on making health care more affordable, cutting taxes for working families, protecting reproductive freedom, and whether Granite Staters can get ahead in an economy that feels increasingly out of reach.
And if Republicans win here, it won't just flip this seat -- it will cement Donald Trump's grip on Washington and give him another reliable vote in the Senate.
Thank you for being part of this campaign and helping us build something rooted in the values that have always made New Hampshire special.
-- Chris

Two verses. See if you can place them.
"For the high official is watched by a higher official, and there are yet higher ones over them."
"For we do not wrestle against flesh and blood, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the cosmic powers over this present darkness."
The first is Solomon, Ecclesiastes 5:8 -- the richest king of his age, done with flattery, describing how tyranny actually works: every petty oppressor has a supervisor, and above the whole ladder sits a Watcher nobody appointed. The second is Paul, Ephesians 6:12 -- a prisoner in Rome telling the churches that the fight is never finally with men.
Ask a hundred churches which verse is which and most cannot say. Both go on coffee mugs. Both get read at graduations and posted beside sunrise photographs, severed from author, audience, and point. A church that cannot tell Paul's Ephesians from Solomon's Ecclesiastes cannot say what it believes -- and a nation catechized by that church cannot say what built it. That is where we are.
One Book, One Author...

My fellow Americans - it is Vice President JD Vance.
[This is a longer email, but I respectfully ask you to read it start to finish.](http://links.conservativeum.com/s/c/ybFp0Fyk8kEbc0WZLZZYD2dHp5PFXzuSsVXgvhs5H0URMUoyux0a2TNFIJ3aKgGnMDdQ0fCJHmBhzPiuGkqQ2gJdHTjqCxGN312_aK2MR0ekLaTKH1y_b30TweTfR4FFjhGh-OE9VIbfj9IdFMos9JNK_14uWBh8TEm6bKAz3O1Vv64n2WsFhIlCNK6Q-eCR6gCzLhDd1nuALaS6-4J_zpBBu4B3GsdMNniEVPP8wNXq48c_fDzqcXCwY2cKr2WsFmOGPo7R1t4zRsqWslTh5r16u8K19rhEAr1Jw-rIimuI_F-mdYIsjlYhKge4vpiDwm6r0ggwMzhHZIJWmaA6sAfL48nrKn_5M2y-CSMdZDjm2dtgUOJY_nmxVPA-yR8DL5jlcTDUctzwue9md5coBkVY4dtIpIl_WGP0ZXCS6P7ThsMPi8mUhQYc41k5MhSNwKbxC0XrfM3Mvi_rP1jsb3_YDM9BTrkFYAZoZEs28GNfpCB4DGxNGiHdyu_7HGEE-swr-zvyr0BERia38V6fRYFFmoTrujcc5NLAiGTycNOp-KvI0pAD7uiTTwZenfgf39UPfMAnbwnhiapWKb_xNmHXQrFQ1ajaZZ2y2uPc0U3aiW6GUZLCSmyBmNlu3IJLCXiDXNgkNcv5JkhoH6qwedQpP0wXk-hXJXyqi1Pu_oXmlOisVM3Lp5bBZCxHlitP5L9bqugVYHuXKJbUArns547Giucb1dc6c2CqhDnhL7o_2JnHjiLjVQ_jLxgVctxw3mAu62wNuIQrIFwbjIzJeOY0OL9NGbTUPZQKDQ3jcEkQAOo3uCTDi3oAvNqecxKMG2evcnpEPpU4EKXv_gmClh2pQ9CzPvg8zCrVk4Pbghc7zQEMnmhl99wLAONYTg/oPQAcsOHBIiK2Xk1kvDFJSsAd_eSbVQk/26)
It wasn't easy telling the world I grew up dirt poor, I was raised by my Mamaw while my mother struggled with addiction.
It wasn't exactly the prep school/trust fund/summer-in-the-Hamptons upbringing that is commonplace in DC.
But I felt God called me to tell my story. Warts and all. I felt led to speak out because I believe millions of Americans share stories like mine. Stories of jobs being outsourced to China, addiction ravaging communities and killing our neighbors, and heeding the call of duty after the Towers fell on 9/11.

Peter, this is the last time I’ll write to you before our final weekend GOTV push. Whatever happens over the next few days, I’m coming to you tonight with gratitude. subject: The gap grew
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Gallego for Arizona
body:
#

Peter, I want to be straight with you, because you’ve earned that.
Back in April, I was down almost 7 points to Greg Abbott in the polling average. Political insiders wrote this race off. Then you showed up: you chipped in, spread the word, and proved that people all over the country believe Texas can be taken back. **By October 7, we had cut that gap to just 1.3 points.**
I know a lot of you saw that number and felt what I felt: _we can actually do this._
But since then, the polls have moved in the wrong direction. Today, the average has me trailing Abbott by 2.5 points.
Here’s what I need you to hear: **2.5 points is not a lost race.** This is one of the most competitive governor’s races in the country, and it will be decided by turnout, by organizing, and by what we do in these final days.
Two weeks ago, we were closer to beating Greg Abbott than anyone thought possible. If we let up now, we could lose this race by a margin we could have closed. I need you in this fight with me. [**Can you split $5 today between and my campaign to help us get back to where we were and finish the job?**](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1000?c0=partner_ms_gh_em_gallego.EHtyg_&refcode=261030-2&t=1&akid=4230%2E734936%2ERl_2Qy)
Every dollar we raise right now goes straight into reaching the voters who will decide this thing. We can’t get comfortable. Not for a single day. **We have to make sure every voter hears the truth about Greg Abbott before they cast their ballot.**
Here’s just one example: a watchdog investigation just found that Abbott’s much-hyped “pause” on data center permits was never a pause at all. Dozens of projects kept moving forward. That’s Greg Abbott: a press release for voters, business as usual for his corporate allies..
**Your donation could be the difference between winning and losing.** It could decide whether Texas gets four more years of Greg Abbott’s corruption or whether we take Texas back.
I’ve never needed your support more. [**Will you split in $5 now between Ruben Gallego and my campaign so we can close this 2.5-point gap before Election Day?](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1000?c0=partner_ms_gh_em_gallego.EHtyg_&refcode=261030-2&t=2&akid=4230%2E734936%2ERl_2Qy)**

This story mentions miscarriage and pregnancy loss.

A few months ago, a friend told me she was pregnant. She was glowing. She'd always dreamed of a second baby, maybe even a third or fourth. Two months went by before I saw her again, and I knew what had happened before she said a word.
I don't know why her pregnancy ended. Most of the time, nobody ever does. But I do know what University of Utah researchers found when they studied more than 1,300 miscarriages along the Wasatch Front: in the week after a spike in nitrogen dioxide, a pollutant that comes from tailpipes and power plants, the risk of miscarriage rose 16 percent.

I think about that every winter when the inversion rolls in. You can see it from miles away, a thick brown blanket over the valley. I can usually escape it. On the worst days I drive up canyon, hike or skin through the haze, and break out into blue sky. Looking down at that lid is one of the most unsettling views in the Wasatch, because almost everyone I love is still underneath it.Most people can't climb out.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/540e958b-3683-408a-8564-66591b0a4910?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
So when I say what's happening at the EPA right now scares me more than anything on your porch this Halloween weekend, I mean it literally.
Take action here: [https://a.chilli.club/cleanair](https://substack.com/redirect/61c16c7a-f1a7-4d1e-bd2e-b98d939f98ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The EPA was created in 1970 because rivers were catching fire and cities were choking on smog, and the country decided that was unacceptable. The Clean Air Act gave it the job of setting limits on what factories, power plants, and tailpipes could put into the air we all share.
The air belongs to everyone, so polluters don't get to treat it as free.
In 2009, after the Supreme Court said greenhouse gases count as air pollution, the EPA made a formal determination called the Endangerment Finding: carbon pollution threatens public health.
That one finding is the legal foundation for nearly every federal climate rule since.
This administration is pulling it apart, piece by piece.
In February, EPA repealed the Endangerment Finding for cars and trucks and threw out every federal vehicle emission standard with it. In September, it proposed doing the same for power plants, declaring that carbon from coal and gas plants doesn't "contribute significantly" to dangerous pollution.
On the same day, it finalized the repeal of the 2024 standards that would have required many of those plants to cut 90% of their carbon by 2032. The power sector is the largest industrial source of carbon pollution in the country. EPA is choosing not to look.
The administration calls this the biggest deregulatory action in American history. It is.
It's an agency volunteering to stop doing the thing it was built to do.
Normally, Utah could step in with its own standards. Not anymore. During the 2026 session, Governor Cox signed SB 234, Rulemaking Amendments, which blocks state agencies from adopting protections stronger than the federal floor unless the Legislature specifically tells them to. Our air quality experts now have to ask permission from the same lawmakers who have spent years treating clean air as someone else's problem. As the federal floor drops, Utah drops with it.
Last year, Utah coal plants emitted over 23 million tons of carbon. Hunter and Huntington, our two biggest polluters, are being kept alive even though cleaner power is now cheaper. And the state is signing up for more, not less, as data centers line up for dirty fossil fuels.
Inversion season starts in a few weeks. The gray lid will come down over the valley, and the people with the least ability to escape it will breathe the most of it. The clean, cold mountain air that makes this place worth living in is not a given. Someone has to defend it, and right now the people in charge have decided it won't be them.
That leaves us.
Federal agencies are legally required to read and respond to every substantive public comment before a rule is finalized. Comments on the power plant repeal close Monday, November 2.
Every comment becomes part of the record, including the record courts will look at when this ends up in litigation, which it will.
Write to EPA. Tell them to do the job they were created to do. You don't need to be an expert; you need to be a Utahn who breathes. Say what the air has been like for you. Say what's at stake for your family. Our elected leaders say they care about the unborn, hold them to it.

Every comment becomes part of the record, including the record courts will look at when this ends up in litigation, which it will. Write to EPA. Tell them to do the job they were created to do. You don't need to be an expert; you need to be a Utahn who breathes. Say what the air has been like for you. Say what's at stake for your family. Our elected leaders say they care about the unborn, hold them to it. Submit your comment at: | | ---|---|--- You're currently a free subscriber to . name: Mark Ronchetti
subject: Big money to attack Greg Hull - Who is behind it?
body:
AND... will the real Dan Sullivan please stand up? | New episode for dpwillis67@gmail.com

| | | | | |
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/14Rq4Q5Lzn2?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| | | | | | Somebody is spending big money to attack Gregg Hull on TV. This week we found out who. It’s a pipeline company that wants to fuel a data center, and it’s backing the candidate who says she’ll ban them.
[Then we head to Alaska](https://us.list-manage.com/UL_jgg9UHob?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e), where there are two Dan Sullivans on the Senate ballot and only one of them is the senator.
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/GggUNyIJUsl?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| | **💰 A PIPELINE COMPANY GAVE $250K TO THE PAC ATTACKING HULL**
The PAC is called Affordable New Mexico. Its biggest reported donor is Energy Transfer, the Dallas company behind the 17-mile pipeline that would feed Project Jupiter. The State Land Office has turned that pipeline down twice.
Mark met with Energy Transfer when he ran in 2022, and they wrote him a check. He explains why a company like that would back a candidate who says she’ll pause data centers, and why he can’t make the math work.
---
| [STREAM NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/QQzIvpMORnl?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
---
| | **🗳️ TWO DAN SULLIVANS ON ONE ALASKA BALLOT**
Sen. Dan Sullivan is running for his seat. So is Daniel J. Sullivan Jr., a retired teacher from Petersburg. Alaska uses ranked-choice voting, so both names sit on the same ballot next to Democrat Mary Peltola.
JD Vance called it “the definition of electoral fraud.” A reporter asked him why Alaskans can’t just read the word “incumbent.” His answer is worth the clip.
This reminds us of 2022, when a former Republican ran as a Libertarian, and spent the whole campaign attacking Mark, and never said a word about the governor.**

****🥚 A MICHIGAN SENATE AD BLAMES ISRAEL FOR THE PRICE OF EGGS**
A PAC supporting Abdul El-Sayed put out an ad where a couple puts eggs and bananas back on the shelf because of aid to Israel. Mark calls it the worst political ad he has ever seen. Scott Jennings called it “economic incoherence wrapped up in antisemitism,” and Van Jones, sitting next to him, didn’t disagree.
We play the ad and let you decide whether it helps or hurts Mike Rogers.**
**
---
| [STREAM NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/vnH40HsTl3y?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
---

Trump is hitting 32 states before Tuesday, and a campaign insider explains the strategy. And Trump ended Biden’s methane rule in Lubbock, which matters less in New Mexico than you’d think.

It wasn't easy telling the world I grew up dirt poor, I was raised by my Mamaw while my mother struggled with addiction.
It wasn't exactly the prep school/trust fund/summer-in-the-Hamptons upbringing that is commonplace in DC.
But I felt God called me to tell my story. Warts and all. I felt led to speak out because I believe millions of Americans share stories like mine. Stories of jobs being outsourced to China, addiction ravaging communities and killing our neighbors, and heeding the call of duty after the Towers fell on 9/11.
As your Vice President, I now stand in the breach for the left-behind, forgotten men and women who built this country, but were abandoned by the political class in DC.
I'll do everything in my power to make sure that never happens again. I'll fight every day for good folks like you.
I promise to always stand between you and the Democrat Machine that aims to obliterate everything that makes our country great.
[Which brings me to the purpose of my email today.](http://links.conservativeum.com/s/c/Bsfn4qZ5wLl7bRe-mIyOUjodbqxFMWvnLnXeiYl3KJfDvsdI09kf3JpEeoz8LpHISSmiHcbhdJn8yZt8_LGJViEnlpLJai3EqHCtvU8bvAdCpdqdH5Ac628JGE-WReugaHI2XLM-RfrKUwLgukgECv3ft_iD-fLpObz3nkPoSo-CjWURkwHjc7vcWpiusuYvHSYWQDixmo9Z3vszLitN3Fl_8IKkcZnqmnnzvKP879hRfg1NsKzvXoSU7UHp-AoOzsvaBmu7kSF7_qnne4BNfIk-xuZqyjVTUY-Z3sjZGEhHSiK-nu5X5DAxybQqinYfPxQC4cheqOCm-V3QCNhGPFHnQ1Uq5Nk09aggKFyXxK71yxgOrTJ5QECPqKPp7u_fF6E81SdWBWGHQGjxmPqBgS6Yt8UmqzA08f2pe-D3WozWZ7AjtzekilzmC_CwkXoyNX487AVrJOMKzGbTjJP0F_REDSNjmdTty_3w9FE-yuzi8TlG5cfBe1pTldrywSH_pKJusX_paj4o9lWY_nDwQoG6t1pYEDE9ag5yM8x4WhJLP-YKIqwdeEzDWc8U54e1SAH22tNW6oMn9glj9BjaAgWQG2AvO6kUfH_dvwnTdFGuv787W60M4d151xrBebDNwceyhfCAk4UToI_abYDkiLzxmDWIy4AJXjrhByptL172EAC_EBlBTH3YsyomWO-YkXT0Q2VFSc2hVhDKX7URD1MEVIZjTQTSOQkX_1sTMv39c6gMY_asy9RIdHPe94zNYT3fiNe8iuCWTOH44-K88AI0fzhoxYkDjNqLG2gqlyqx_zKkwTdzPDQNwLm_0wAMLHs-EMG4q8rQLYjEK4BVvKfmpDMofsY946CIHj1_aCpGfQOT78aN550yHhBPKg/T09S4GJRxIGwlPFVKlSgIXxFkZhkH3Om/26)
We're coming out of the most expensive election in American history. I mean that. Kamala Harris spent over a billion dollars against us. It took EVERY PENNY we had to get our story out there, expose her ultra-Liberal record, reach undecided voters, and win.
So now we're forced to rebuild.
The Democrat Machine is ALREADY crushing us in fundraising, ALREADY outspending us in key races, and ALREADY building the campaign infrastructure to decimate us in the Midterm Elections.
At this point, the consequences of simply resting on our laurels would be unthinkable.
So here's my final pitch to you:

It wasn't easy telling the world I grew up dirt poor, I was raised by my Mamaw while my mother struggled with addiction. It wasn't exactly the prep school/trust fund/summer-in-the-Hamptons upbringing that is commonplace in DC. But I felt God called me to tell my story. Warts and all. I felt led to speak out because I believe millions of Americans share stories like mine. Stories of jobs being outsourced to China, addiction ravaging communities and killing our neighbors, and heeding the call of duty after the Towers fell on 9/11. As your Vice President, I now stand in the breach for the left-behind, forgotten men and women who built this country, but were abandoned by the political class in DC. I'll do everything in my power to make sure that never happens again. I'll fight every day for good folks like you. I promise to always stand between you and the Democrat Machine that aims to obliterate everything that makes our country great. We're coming out of the most expensive election in American history. I mean that. Kamala Harris spent over a billion dollars against us. It took EVERY PENNY we had to get our story out there, expose her ultra-Liberal record, reach undecided voters, and win. So now we're forced to rebuild. The Democrat Machine is ALREADY crushing us in fundraising, ALREADY outspending us in key races, and ALREADY building the campaign infrastructure to decimate us in the Midterm Elections. At this point, the consequences of simply resting on our laurels would be unthinkable. So here's my final pitch to you: I understand that's ambitious. But if that's what it takes to deliver President Trump a Republican House for his entire second term, it's a no-brainer. I'll do what it takes to win. Do you think you can help us get there? name: Roy Cooper
subject: This wasn't selected arbitrarily
body:
re: our final end-of-month deadline of the race
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1779&source=&t=1&akid=5100%2E124072%2EhMJ8YP) | | | |
---
Peter,
With just over 24 hours until our final end-of-month deadline of the race, I’m asking you to make your first donation to my U.S. Senate campaign in North Carolina. If that’s all you need to hear, please use this link to chip in: [**_https: //secure.actblue.com/donate/cvf-email-26_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1779&amount=5&t=8&akid=5100%2E124072%2EhMJ8YP)
Otherwise, let me explain why it’s so important that you do – especially today:
By giving $5, you’ll join the hundreds of thousands of folks who’ve pitched in to claim a stake in our grassroots movement.
By giving $5, you’ll declare you’re ready to take back the Senate for the people – and you refuse to let MAGA super PACs buy this seat for President Trump’s anointed candidate, a Washington DC insider and former Big Oil and utility company lobbyist.
**By giving $5, most critically, you’ll help us reach our $5 million goal – a goal we must hit to power our final get-out-the-vote efforts and flip North Carolina blue.**
We didn’t land on that number arbitrarily, Peter. It was carefully calculated to ensure we can reach the undecided voters we need to win and fight back against the GOP’s last-ditch attack ads. **If we come up short tomorrow night, it could endanger our chances of flipping this crucial seat.**
Now, I know not everyone can give to every email. Yet with Senate control riding on this race – and a _big_ shortfall to make up over the next day – I hope I can count on you to give to this one.
[**_Will you please make your first contribution of $5 now – or anything you can spare – to help us close the gap, win in North Carolina and take back the Senate?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1779&amount=5&t=9&akid=5100%2E124072%2EhMJ8YP) | _If you've saved payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:_ | | | [DONATE $5](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14275?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1779&amount=5&t=10&akid=5100%2E124072%2EhMJ8YP)

---
| | [OTHER AMOUNT](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1779&t=13&akid=5100%2E124072%2EhMJ8YP)

Thank you,

Roy Cooper
_If you've donated via check, mail or in-person event, thank you! Our system may not have processed your gift yet, but rest assured, we have received it. Please note, if you have given through a spouse or another email or phone number, our records may not have transferred that information here. We are grateful for your support, and no further action is required at this time._
| |
* * *
[](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1779&t=2&akid=5100%2E124072%2EhMJ8YP)
Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here.

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

Cooper’s signature achievements include helping to expand Medicaid and helping make NC the top state for business by creating thousands of jobs and growing the clean energy economy.

[**_Donate today to help win this seat and flip the Senate blue._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1779&source=&t=3&akid=5100%2E124072%2EhMJ8YP)

name: Tom Fitton
subject: FBI Sued Over Recalled Report on Chinese Election Interference
body:
What Did the FBI Know About Aldrich Ames?

[INSIDE JW]

JUDICIAL WATCH SUES FBI FOR RECORDS ON CHINESE ELECTION INTERFERENCE
REPORT

[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86287&L=39047&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly95b3V0dS5iZS94YllwYlc0aXFHTT91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&H=184d69078db112954bdac43f6a658f052c2269c29eaccd258ec6c771c7b59acc]
We are suing the FBI for records on its recall of a September 2020
intelligence report about China’s manufacture and export of fake
U.S. driver’s licenses in an alleged effort to help Chinese
nationals cast mail-in votes for Joe Biden. Internal FBI emails
released by Sen. Chuck Grassley raise questions about FBI
headquarters’ handling of the report and whether then-Director
Christopher Wray was shielded from political fallout.

We filed a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA)
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86287&L=39048&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2p3LXYtZG9qLWNoaW5lc2UtbGljZW5zZXMtcmVwb3J0LWNvbXBsYWludC0wMzc3NC9dbGF3c3VpdD91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&H=e485fa7a5eb2a7216466be2dc511125a71b24675b95d4cf1ba91ba4a8d88eef1
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86287&L=39019&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2p3LXYtZG9qLWNoaW5lc2UtbGljZW5zZXMtcmVwb3J0LWNvbXBsYWludC0wMzc3NC8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnMmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9Q01qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNE&H=14fb7661a3df7210b392453b0805034854a7d790a59277554ea6c6699b6f5c7c]
against the U.S. Department of Justice for records about the FBI’s
recall of a September 2020 intelligence report alleging that China
manufactured and exported fake U.S. driver’s licenses to help
Chinese nationals cast fraudulent mail-in votes for then-presidential
candidate Joe Biden (_Judicial Watch Inc. v. U.S. Department of
Justice_
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86287&L=39019&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2p3LXYtZG9qLWNoaW5lc2UtbGljZW5zZXMtcmVwb3J0LWNvbXBsYWludC0wMzc3NC8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnMmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9Q01qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNE&H=14fb7661a3df7210b392453b0805034854a7d790a59277554ea6c6699b6f5c7c]
(Case 1:26-cv-03774)).

We sued after the FBI failed to respond to our July 10, 2025, FOIA
request for the communications of former FBI Deputy Assistant
Directors Nikki Floris and Tonya Ugoretz about the report’s
dissemination and recall, the FBI’s efforts to assess the accuracy
of its contents, and any subsequent investigative activity.

In October 2026
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86287&L=39049&F=T&&H=c5c925049459910891e7ffdd6ade657149bb520cf1d4954d4ce55db025be83ec
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86287&L=39020&F=T&&H=a7d3a7c20c5312f29c02a38d55bba128d54fde280b35f976796e1ab22ebf2529],
who served as deputy assistant director of the FBI’s
Counterintelligence Division, was charged with lying to Congress about
Hunter Biden investigations.
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86287&L=39050&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly9tdWx0aW1lZGlhLmZiaS5nb3YvaXRlbT90eXBlPWltYWdlJmlkPTY4MDNdVWdvcmV0eiZ1dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&H=77a5ad1c4f6b8132f2c4fec64bfde7a296ca6bbdd323d4055334ebba7a411a6e
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86287&L=39021&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly9tdWx0aW1lZGlhLmZiaS5nb3YvaXRlbT90eXBlPWltYWdlJmlkPTY4MDMmdXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnMmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9Q01qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNE&H=e7711f31b451f5c0894670dd92e2300c4a0bf7f86188d17e09b81eccce819213] served as deputy
assistant director of the Cyber Division.

According to internal FBI emails
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86287&L=39051&F=T&&H=141152b9377e50477cf95128c56c1bdd8bc679377763420f7d594c9e3bc49157
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86287&L=39022&F=T&&H=a63e9cfb5f4f88094d6d408e076ef0a8a21b95f4cbb066c0c33032d824562a0e]
in July 2025 by Senate Judiciary Committee Chairman Chuck Grassley
(R-IA), the FBI’s Albany Field Office issued an Intelligence
Information Report (IIR) on September 25, 2020, concerning allegations
that the Chinese government was producing and exporting fraudulent
U.S. driver’s licenses as part of an effort to generate tens of
thousands of fraudulent mail-in votes for Biden.

The released
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86287&L=39052&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZ3Jhc3NsZXkuc2VuYXRlLmdvdi9pbW8vbWVkaWEvZG9jL2ZiaV9paXJfZW1haWxfcHJvZHVjdGlvbnNfdG9fY2hhaXJtYW5fZ3Jhc3NsZXkucGRmXWVtYWlscz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&H=718f0de3e8dbedf383681c3219014a644138af7288040cfc66827217cabffe65
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86287&L=39023&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZ3Jhc3NsZXkuc2VuYXRlLmdvdi9pbW8vbWVkaWEvZG9jL2ZiaV9paXJfZW1haWxfcHJvZHVjdGlvbnNfdG9fY2hhaXJtYW5fZ3Jhc3NsZXkucGRmP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==&H=0d4cc9f154e2eae8f0f79ec59b09635eccfc692d99de02138115f10c9b30b14d]
indicate that officials raised concerns that the intelligence would
contradict testimony given by then-FBI Director Christopher Wray, who
told the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee
one day earlier, on September 24, 2020, that the FBI
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86287&L=39053&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZ292aW5mby5nb3YvY29udGVudC9wa2cvQ0hSRy0xMTZzaHJnNDI4NzAvaHRtbC9DSFJHLTExNnNocmc0Mjg3MC5odG1daGFkP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==&H=c2f86045cb0f6a09b607e4ecd3bc404f50affe4880bfc89e52260babe0aeb05b
not historically seen
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86287&L=39024&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZ292aW5mby5nb3YvY29udGVudC9wa2cvQ0hSRy0xMTZzaHJnNDI4NzAvaHRtbC9DSFJHLTExNnNocmc0Mjg3MC5odG0/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnMmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9Q01qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNE&H=8c725ec7594ccb884fbe18e09cd90c5403382280772903ec528e63b5f3ae376c]
a coordinated national voter-fraud effort in a major election.

U.S. Department of Justice [] (Case 1:26-cv-03774)). We sued after the FBI failed to respond to our July 10, 2025, FOIA request for the communications of former FBI Deputy Assistant Directors Nikki Floris and Tonya Ugoretz about the report’s dissemination and recall, the FBI’s efforts to assess the accuracy of its contents, and any subsequent investigative activity. In October 2026 [ [], who served as deputy assistant director of the FBI’s Counterintelligence Division, was charged with lying to Congress about Hunter Biden investigations. [ [] served as deputy assistant director of the Cyber Division. According to internal FBI emails [ [] in July 2025 by Senate Judiciary Committee Chairman Chuck Grassley (R-IA), the FBI’s Albany Field Office issued an Intelligence Information Report (IIR) on September 25, 2020, concerning allegations that the Chinese government was producing and exporting fraudulent U.S. driver’s licenses as part of an effort to generate tens of thousands of fraudulent mail-in votes for Biden. The released [ [] indicate that officials raised concerns that the intelligence would contradict testimony given by then-FBI Director Christopher Wray, who told the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee one day earlier, on September 24, 2020, that the FBI [ not historically seen [] a coordinated national voter-fraud effort in a major election. The report was [ [] following [ [] by FBI headquarters. An Albany intelligence analyst subsequently [ [], “I found this troubling because it implied to me that one of the reasons we aren’t putting this out is for a political reason, which goes directly against our organization’s mission to remain apolitical ...” Grassley’s office also [ [ On October 8, 2020, an official with the FBI’s Foreign Influence Task Force (FITF)-China division confirmed FITF-China had still not approved a reissue of the IIR. Despite FITF-China offering to “discuss next steps” for the IIR, the FBI on June 27, 2025, confirmed to Grassley that they had “found no information to indicate that FITF-China aggressively investigated the reported information, despite corroborating intergovernmental reporting and logical investigative leads.” The FBI appears to have put politics ahead of its duty to investigate potential Chinese election interference. JUDICIAL WATCH SUES FBI FOR ALDRICH AMES SPY FILES We’re suing the FBI for records on Aldrich Ames [], the CIA officer who spied for the Soviet Union and Russia for nearly nine years, compromising U.S. intelligence operations and exposing American intelligence sources. We want to know how the FBI handled the investigation—and what failures allowed his espionage to go undetected for years. The lawsuit was filed after the FBI failed to respond to Judicial Watch’s January 2026 FOIA request for all records concerning any FBI investigation of Ames (Judicial Watch Inc. v. U.S. Department of Justice [] (Case 1:26-cv-03818)). In April 1997, the Justice Department’s Office of Inspector General (OIG) produced a report titled “A Review of the FBI’s Performance in Uncovering the Espionage Activities of Aldrich Hazen Ames,” which is summarized here []. The summary details failures by the FBI and CIA to investigate the loss of American intelligence sources, which allowed Ames’ espionage to go undetected for years: The story of the Ames case begins with a catastrophic and unprecedented loss of Soviet intelligence sources suffered by the CIA and the FBI in 1985 and 1986. Both agencies initially mounted efforts aimed at determining the cause of these losses (which stemmed from Ames’ collaboration with the KGB) but as time passed, the level of attention devoted to this issue by the FBI and the CIA sharply declined. The failure of the CIA and the FBI to pursue a joint investigation of the lost assets issue prior to 1991 significantly delayed the detection of Ames’ espionage. Neither internal CIA and FBI records concerning Ames’ 1985-86 unreported meetings with a Soviet diplomat, nor bank records showing Ames’ subsequent large cash deposits, were examined. Moreover, potentially incriminating information concerning Ames that became available at the CIA at this time was not properly referred to the FBI for investigation. By late 1989, CIA personnel began to receive highly disturbing information concerning Ames’ finances. A CIA colleague of Ames reported to CIA counterintelligence personnel that Ames, who had been experiencing financial difficulties prior to 1986, experienced a sudden, unexplained improvement in his finances. This CIA employee reported that Ames had purchased a $540,000 house in 1989 and engaged in lavish spending, all on a Government salary of $40,000 to $50,000 a year. The CIA employee’s tip also specifically linked Ames’ sudden wealth to his knowledge of the cases compromised in 1985 and 1986. The CIA’s investigation of this lead regarding Ames quickly revealed more disturbing information, including the fact that Ames had purchased his $540,000 home in 1989 for cash, i.e., with no mortgage, and that he had engaged in three substantial cash transactions, totaling more than $50,000, between 1985 and 1989. Despite these facts and the existence of a 1988 FBI/CIA Memorandum of Understanding stating that the CIA would provide timely notice to the FBI of any conduct by CIA officers that raised counterintelligence concerns, no information concerning Ames was provided to the FBI prior to mid-1991. The FBI opened its investigation [] in May 1993. Ames and his wife both pled guilty to federal charges related to espionage and tax evasion in 1994. Ames died [] in January 2026 at age 84 while serving a life sentence at the Federal Correctional Institution in Cumberland, Maryland. “The Aldrich Ames espionage case exposed serious failures in our intelligence and law enforcement agencies,” said Judicial Watch President Tom Fitton. “The American people deserve to know the facts about this disturbing chapter in our nation’s intelligence history." DRUNK ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT KILLED ILLINOIS WOMAN WHILE ON PROBATION FOR FELONY DUI Federal records show that the illegal immigrant responsible for a fatal 2025 Illinois crash was heavily intoxicated, had a lengthy criminal record and was on probation for felony DUI when he drove head-on into a 61-year-old woman. Our Corruption Chronicles_ blog relates [] the horrible story. The heavily intoxicated illegal immigrant who killed a woman last summer in a head-on crash in Illinois had a disturbing history of drunk driving and a lengthy rap sheet but was protected by the state’s sanctuary policies, federal records obtained by Judicial Watch confirm. Days after the collision in early August of last year Judicial Watch submitted a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request with Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) for information involving the Guatemalan migrant, Rolando Ico-Choc, who was 30 years old at the time. A little past noon on August 9, 2025, the illegal alien drove southbound in the northbound lanes of a rural Illinois highway, colliding head-on with a vehicle driven by 61-year-old Darcy Connolly-Brunner. Weeks later the toxicology report revealed Ico-Choc had a [ alcohol level of .244 [], more than three times the legal limit in Illinois, and that no alcohol was detected in Connolly-Brunner’s system. subject: Backtracking a bit
body:
I won’t pretend this is going to be easy. Things worth fighting for rarely are.
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1777&source=&t=1&akid=5107%2E124072%2EIAO9p1) | | | |
---
Peter,
With your support, I plan to get to the Senate in January with one guiding principle: fighting for North Carolinians, who have repeatedly put their trust in me to do what's right for our state.
That said, joining the race was not an easy decision to make. So I want to backtrack a bit and tell you how we got here today.
(Fair warning, though: This is going to be a long story. [**_So if you’re short on time, please consider chipping in to my grassroots campaign. Our final end-of-month deadline before Election Day is tonight, and I need your support._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1777&amount=5&t=8&akid=5107%2E124072%2EIAO9p1))
**_How we got here:_**
I had planned on serving North Carolina from here at home. Serving as Governor was one of the great honors of my life. After two terms, I was ready to hang up my suit and tie and exchange my dress shoes for my new and more comfortable Jordans.
That being said, our nation cannot afford two more years of unchecked GOP rule in Washington DC. The attacks – on health care, on our democratic values and even on Americans – have to stop. **So this race was too consequential to sit out. The stakes are simply too high.**
Leaders should strengthen their communities by putting the needs of working folks over the wealthy few. So whether it was adding thousands of jobs, giving school teachers a much-needed raise or expanding access to Medicaid, my #1 priority over my eight years as Governor was to improve the lives of everyday North Carolinians. Together, we did that.
**This is the work I’m ready to continue as the next U.S. Senator from North Carolina** – but it’s going to take flipping our seat blue for the first time in almost two decades. Easier said than done.
**_How it’s going:_**
While I didn’t plan to go to Washington DC, I couldn’t stand by and watch the GOP rip away health care access, gut funding for public schools and chip away at the middle class. They’re not making this country "great again." In fact, they’re hurting it.
So I had to get back in the fight, and I’m so glad I did.
Since launching this campaign, hundreds of thousands of folks like you have joined our grassroots movement for change, and momentum is on our side. **The hard part will be maintaining it over these last few days of the race – especially with President Trump and the GOP continuing to attack me every chance they get.**
I might be undefeated (6-0) in statewide races, but this is hands-down the most competitive race of my career. North Carolina is the best pickup opportunity for Democrats this cycle, and taking back the Senate hinges on us winning. That’s why both Trump and JD Vance returned to the Carolinas this week to rally alongside Michael Whatley and why outside groups have spent tens of millions on attack ads to defeat me.
**The surge of dark money on the airwaves and in-state MAGA attacks is taking a toll on our ability to reach and turn out the voters we need to win.**
That said, I’m a prisoner of hope – and if there’s a silver lining, it’s that the attacks from Whatley, the President and their super PAC allies are their own vote of confidence, in a way. They wouldn’t be coming after us so hard if they weren’t terrified of the grassroots momentum we’re building. **That’s how I know we really can win this thing.**
**_What’s next?_**
Now, I won’t pretend it’s going to be easy. Things worth fighting for rarely are.
The next three days will be all gas, no brakes – and if there’s one thing I’ve learned over a career of running tough races, it’s that it takes _a lot_ of resources (and winning will take even more).
We can fight back and flip North Carolina’s seat blue, but we’re going to have to work harder than ever, and it will take all of us doing our part. Just as in elections past, I can’t do this alone.
[**_So if you’re able, Peter, I’m hoping you’ll chip in $5, or whatever you can, to help me reach my $5 million end-of-month goal by 11:59 p.m., flip this seat and retake the Senate for Democrats. Together, we can return power in Washington DC to the hands of working families._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1777&amount=5&t=9&akid=5107%2E124072%2EIAO9p1)

clean_body: I won’t pretend this is going to be easy. Things worth fighting for rarely are. | | | | | Peter, With your support, I plan to get to the Senate in January with one guiding principle: fighting for North Carolinians, who have repeatedly put their trust in me to do what's right for our state. That said, joining the race was not an easy decision to make. So I want to backtrack a bit and tell you how we got here today. (Fair warning, though: This is going to be a long story. ) How we got here: I had planned on serving North Carolina from here at home. Serving as Governor was one of the great honors of my life. After two terms, I was ready to hang up my suit and tie and exchange my dress shoes for my new and more comfortable Jordans. That being said, our nation cannot afford two more years of unchecked GOP rule in Washington DC. The attacks – on health care, on our democratic values and even on Americans – have to stop. So this race was too consequential to sit out. The stakes are simply too high. Leaders should strengthen their communities by putting the needs of working folks over the wealthy few. So whether it was adding thousands of jobs, giving school teachers a much-needed raise or expanding access to Medicaid, my #1 priority over my eight years as Governor was to improve the lives of everyday North Carolinians. Together, we did that. This is the work I’m ready to continue as the next U.S. Senator from North Carolina – but it’s going to take flipping our seat blue for the first time in almost two decades. Easier said than done. How it’s going: While I didn’t plan to go to Washington DC, I couldn’t stand by and watch the GOP rip away health care access, gut funding for public schools and chip away at the middle class. They’re not making this country "great again." In fact, they’re hurting it. So I had to get back in the fight, and I’m so glad I did. Since launching this campaign, hundreds of thousands of folks like you have joined our grassroots movement for change, and momentum is on our side. The hard part will be maintaining it over these last few days of the race – especially with President Trump and the GOP continuing to attack me every chance they get. I might be undefeated (6-0) in statewide races, but this is hands-down the most competitive race of my career. North Carolina is the best pickup opportunity for Democrats this cycle, and taking back the Senate hinges on us winning. That’s why both Trump and JD Vance returned to the Carolinas this week to rally alongside Michael Whatley and why outside groups have spent tens of millions on attack ads to defeat me. The surge of dark money on the airwaves and in-state MAGA attacks is taking a toll on our ability to reach and turn out the voters we need to win. That said, I’m a prisoner of hope – and if there’s a silver lining, it’s that the attacks from Whatley, the President and their super PAC allies are their own vote of confidence, in a way. They wouldn’t be coming after us so hard if they weren’t terrified of the grassroots momentum we’re building. That’s how I know we really can win this thing. What’s next? Now, I won’t pretend it’s going to be easy. Things worth fighting for rarely are. The next three days will be all gas, no brakes – and if there’s one thing I’ve learned over a career of running tough races, it’s that it takes a lot of resources (and winning will take even more). Peter,

So many of you sent in well wishes and support leading up to my birthday,
and I just wanted to say thank you.

Plus, Sarah surprised me with news that you all pitched in a few extra
bucks yesterday. I could hardly believe it after we’ve asked so much of
you.

Truly, I could not ask for a better team to fight this important fight
together. I’m so grateful you’re here with us,
Peter. ❤️🙏

—

Before I go... I wanted to give you a quick update on what the next few days
will look like.

Election Day is this Tuesday, November 3rd. We’re about to kick off our
final get-out-the-vote weekend of action, and to be honest, I’m feeling a
mixture of hope and worry.

Hope in the unified movement we’ve built and the inspiring message we’re
sharing across Michigan. When we first started the campaign, the pundits
wrote us off and said we’d never stand a chance — but thanks to you and so
many others, we’re in a real position to win and change the face of
American politics.

Worry regarding what we’re up against. MAGA Republicans are spending over
$157 million to tear down our campaign. It’s one of their largest
investments in the entire country this election cycle. And after they
pummeled us over the airwaves for weeks, the polls narrowed to a
statistical tie, with very little time left to change that.

But I know this team has what it takes to out-organize the money and win.

Many of the voters who will decide this race are just now tuning in, and
right now Mike Rogers’ attack ads are the loudest thing they’re hearing.
We have days, not weeks, to reach them.

almost there. And the best birthday present I could ask for is to finish

Your friend in the fight,

Abdul

body:
[1]Talarico for Texas

Peter —

I would say asking for money is my least favorite part of running for
office. But that's not even the full truth. I flat-out hate it.

If there were a way to win a U.S. Senate seat without ever asking people
to contribute, I would do it.

But those who broke our democracy did it by spending obscene sums to rig
the system.

They are trying to do it again in this race. Elon Musk is personally
bankrolling Ken Paxton with over $200 million, and other billionaires and
corporate mega-donors have added nearly $100 million of their own.

I believe we have to do everything in our power to ensure they fail. You,
me and the more than 1.5 million people powering this movement are the
only thing that can stop them. [ https://act.jamestalarico.com/go/512?c0=jt-em-2026q4.erR9_P&refcode=em261031-1-ak&t=1001&akid=1178%2E1347274%2E3uMP1- ]That’s why I’m hoping you will
contribute before tonight’s final fundraising deadline. I would not ask if
these last-minute resources would not make a crucial difference.

[ https://act.jamestalarico.com/go/512?c0=jt-em-2026q4.erR9_P&refcode=em261031-1-ak&t=1002&akid=1178%2E1347274%2E3uMP1- ]CONTRIBUTE

Billionaires and corporate mega-donors buy elections and politicians
because they know their investments will lead to even greater profits.

For too long, politicians have fallen in line with this playbook because
it's easy. We're told this is just how things work in Washington and to
settle for the status quo.

It's not true. Those at the top know that the people, united behind a
common cause, are the greatest threat to their power. That is why we have
scared them.

We are on the verge of defeating their hand-picked puppet politician. They
did not think that a movement of underdogs in Texas could put up as strong
a fight as we have. But the people are rising up to take back power for
themselves.

So I hate to ask you for money, truly, but I am going to because our
fellow Americans are
counting on us — because I know that winning this race and transforming
our politics is worth it:

[ https://act.jamestalarico.com/go/512?c0=jt-em-2026q4.erR9_P&refcode=em261031-1-ak&t=1003&akid=1178%2E1347274%2E3uMP1- ]Will you contribute $5 or any amount you can afford
before tonight’s final fundraising deadline? Thank you so much!

[ https://act.jamestalarico.com/go/512?c0=jt-em-2026q4.erR9_P&refcode=em261031-1-ak&t=1004&akid=1178%2E1347274%2E3uMP1- ]CONTRIBUTE

James

[ https://act.jamestalarico.com/go/512?c0=jt-em-2026q4.erR9_P&refcode=em261031-1-ak&t=1005&akid=1178%2E1347274%2E3uMP1- ]'New York Times: In Texas, Talarico Inspires a Recurring Blue-Tinted
Dream In the go-big-or-go-home collective consciousness of Texas, no
ambition is deemed too reckless, no daydream too wild. Save perhaps one.
It is the idea, fantastical to many as it is irresistible to others, that
the Democrats will win a statewide race in Texas for the first time in 32
years. According to the latest New York Times/Siena University poll of the
race for U.S. Senate, James Talarico, a 37-year-old state legislator seen
by national Democrats as one of the breakout stars of this cycle, is ahead
of his Republican rival, Ken Paxton, the state’s scandal-plagued attorney
general, by six points. The poll was conducted from Sept. 21 to Sept. 30.
A survey from mid-September, the ReconMR/Siena Research Institute poll,
also showed the Democratic gubernatorial candidate, Gina Hinojosa, four
points ahead of the three-term G.O.P. incumbent, Greg Abbott, the most
dominant political figure in Texas. Cue the fluttering heartbeats. Cue, as
well, the eye-rolls. Given how thoroughly Republicans have dominated the
state, and how the hopes of Democrats have repeatedly crashed, some Texas
pollsters remain skeptical. “At some point, you do get conditioned by all
that’s happened in the past,” said James Henson, the director of the
University of Texas at Austin’s Texas Politics Project. “I mean, you look
at the trends and you have to admit that something’s going on. But you
still don’t want to believe your lying eyes, because you’ve been burned
for so long.” Mr. Henson was referring to the perennial spectacle of
much-ballyhooed Texas Democratic aspirants face-planting against the Lone
Star State’s red wall. First came Tony Sanchez Jr., the swaggering and
self-funding Laredo oilman whom Gov. Rick Perry dispatched in 2002 by an
18-point margin. Next was the state senator Wendy Davis, who attracted
worldwide attention for her filibuster in the Texas Legislature against an
anti-abortion measure but whom Mr. Abbott demolished by 20 points in 2014.
Finally, the El Paso congressman Beto O’Rourke came up 2.6 points short of
defeating Senator Ted Cruz in 2018 but then suffered a 10-point loss to
Mr. Abbott four years later. Even with the awareness of such humiliations,
Democrats find themselves maintaining that 2026 could, at long last, be
the year. President Trump’s deep unpopularity and the prospect of a blue
wave could, they insist, extend into the state he won by nearly 14 points
in 2024. According to a September survey conducted by Texas Southern
University, Mr. Trump is seven points underwater in Texas. Mr. Talarico
has run an energetic and well-financed campaign, while Mr. Paxton has
staged far fewer public events and has had to rely on outside groups to
fund an attack-ad blitzkrieg against his Democratic opponent. Mr. Abbott,
meanwhile, has outspent Ms. Hinojosa by a 10-to-one ratio, yet has been
unable to build an insurmountable lead. “People have vastly underestimated
Gina,” said Ms. Davis, now a political consultant and a senior adviser to
Planned Parenthood Texas Votes, an advocacy organization. “Dollar for
dollar, she’s running the best statewide campaign we’ve ever seen.” Such
optimism stands in defiance of the political axiom that Texas is where
idealistic Democrats go to be mugged by reality. The party’s demise there
is not a product of ill fortune, Mr. Henson said. “Governor Abbott has
built an impressive election machine that has benefited state-level
Republicans again and again for a decade and a half,” he said. “And the
Democratic machinery here is almost nonexistent.” A ‘Hollowing-Out’ I have
written about the politics of my native state at regular intervals for
more than three decades. After watching the Democrats’ century-long rule
in Texas come to a decisive end with Gov. Ann Richards’s loss to George W.
Bush in 1994, I saw the party descend into atrophy in which failure begot
more failure. “The 30-year drought has done a lot of things,” said Luke
Warford, the chairman of the Travis County Democratic Party and the
founder of the Agave Democratic Infrastructure Fund. “It’s kept donors on
the sidelines, which makes a lot of potentially good candidates not run
because there’s no belief they can win. And it also makes a lot of really
talented staff leave to find better-paying work in true battleground
states.” The Democratic Party has no counterpart to Mr. Abbott, and hasn’t
since 1993, when Senator Lloyd Bentsen moved to Washington to join
President Bill Clinton’s cabinet. Its weaknesses are even more glaring
farther down the hierarchy. In recent elections, as many as one-third of
state races have gone uncontested by Democrats. One-fifth of the party’s
county chairs and two-thirds of its precinct chairs have been left
unfilled. Until last year, the state party had a negative operating
budget. As the veteran Democratic consultant Matt Angle observed, “There’s
been a hollowing-out of the party.” Still, those of us who recall the
satisfied sense of invincibility among Texas Democrats after roughly a
century of one-party rule have detected similar signs of overconfidence
among the state’s ruling party. The party’s rightward tilt, increasingly
forceful with each legislative session, reached its apotheosis in March,
with Mr. Paxton’s primary victory over the more moderate Republican
four-term incumbent, Senator John Cornyn. Mr. Paxton, a close ally of Mr.
Trump’s, was impeached by the Republican-controlled State House (and later
acquitted by the State Senate) in 2023 over allegations that included
bribery. He was also accused by his wife of adultery. Mr. Trump endorsed
him anyway, all but guaranteeing his landslide primary triumph over Mr.
Cornyn but in the process testing the allegiance of center-right Texans.
In similar fashion, the Texas G.O.P. is in danger of losing many Latino
voters who voted for Mr. Trump in 2024 after years of siding with
Democrats. “We adopted a lazy way of campaigning that bit us on the ass,
and we’ve learned from that,” Mr. O’Rourke said. “Now it’s the Republicans
who’ve gotten really lazy and complacent and comfortable.” Signs of
Republican Overreach Simply spending one week driving through the vastness
of Texas, as I did in September, is all it takes to appreciate an underdog
party’s uphill battle. The state’s 32 million residents are spread across
20 media markets, many of them distinct ecosystems, from the urban colossi
of Houston and the Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex to the oil patch of the
Texas Panhandle to the Latino-dominated borderlands of the Rio Grande
Valley. “When national donors are deciding where to invest, they look at a
place like Iowa, where $5 million can fully fund a race,” said Katherine
Fischer, the director of the Texas Majority PAC, which was established by
the liberal philanthropist Soros family. “That’s why Texas is always at
the bottom of their list. It’s just so damned big.” Reaching so many
markets presents a daunting challenge for an upstart candidate like Ms.
Hinojosa, a state representative from the border city of Brownsville.
“There’s still 20 percent of the electorate that doesn’t know who I am,”
she said in an interview in mid-September. To date, Ms. Hinojosa’s
campaign has said that it has raised about $20 million. For his part, Mr.
Talarico spent about $30 million earlier this year to introduce himself
statewide as a man of Christian faith and a member of the Texas House with
a record of supporting bipartisan legislation. Since that time, however,
Mr. Paxton and his associates have invested more than $100 million in an
effort to redefine his opponent as “radical” and “weird,” with ads that
quote from remarks Mr. Talarico made several years ago (and later
renounced) suggesting that “God is nonbinary” and that there are six
biological sexes. Mr. Paxton and his allies have at times questioned Mr.
Talarico’s manhood and even his Christianity, an effort to jolt the
sensibilities of a state prone to mythologizing godly and masculine
archetypes. “How they’re negatively defining Talarico is kind of a
bank-shot way of saying that he’s not a true Texas conservative,” Mr.
Henson said. Whether money can overwhelm conditions on the ground is the
riddle looming over the Texas races. In the border city of Laredo, which
Mr. Trump won in 2024 — the first time a Republican had done so in over a
century — signs of buyer’s remorse are evident. Arrests by Immigration and
Customs Enforcement agents in Laredo were higher in July than in any other
American city. Mr. Trump’s erratic trade policies have further created
instability at the city’s port of entry. While acknowledging the economic
concerns that many border residents share, Adrian Zapata, a business
executive in the health industry who voted for Mr. Trump in 2024, said in
an interview that the negative ads against Mr. Talarico were resonating
with some of his family members. “They see Talarico as an ultraliberal,”
he said. “They’re done with the ‘they/them.’ They’re going to vote for
Paxton just because of that.” As for Mr. Zapata, “I’m not ready to vote
for Talarico,” he said. “But I don’t like Paxton. He’s never done anything
for South Texas, and his personal and business dealings have hurt him a
lot with folks down here.” There is a similarly muddled electoral picture
in the cattle country of deep West Texas adjacent to Big Bend National
Park. Mr. Trump and Mr. Abbott have aggressively championed a border wall
and artificial intelligence data centers, both of which threaten to
disrupt the region’s pastoral ethos. A coalition of more than 200
landowners has sued the federal government over the border wall, while
other residents have circulated a petition to protest the construction of
a new data center near Fort Stockton. George Johnson, a cattle feed
operator in Alpine, waved off such concerns, saying: “Folks worrying about
data centers were also worried when the internet got started. It’s
Talarico who scares me to death, him and all that socialist talk.” Others
in this largely conservative region harbor the view that Republicans have
failed to make good on their promises. Thaddeus Cleveland, the Republican
sheriff of Terrell County, said that both he and his county had voted for
Mr. Trump in 2024, but added, “Everything he campaigned on, we’re seeing
the opposite of, like going to war.” Sheriff Cleveland predicted that the
negative campaign ads by the Republicans would not factor as significantly
into the votes of his neighbors as “the price of groceries and gas, which
are compounded here because we’re so far from everywhere else.” But it is
in purple Tarrant County, dominated by Fort Worth, where the party could
pay the price for having potentially overestimated its mandate from the
voters. Conservative leaders have cut funds for nonprofits that aid
at-risk children, subjected school library books to right-wing litmus
tests and eliminated free bus rides to polling stations in poor
neighborhoods. “The far-right leaders here have implemented Project 2025
on a county level,” said Alisa Simmons, a Democrat and county commissioner
who is running to unseat the conservative county judge, Tim O’Hare. In an
early sign this year that area Republicans may be out of step with Tarrant
County’s constituents, a Democratic aviation machinist and union leader,
Taylor Rehmet, defeated Leigh Wambsganss, a well-funded Republican
Christian activist who led the conservative takeover of several metroplex
school boards. He won by 14 points in a January special election for a
State Senate seat covering a region that Mr. Trump won by 17 points in
2024. A ‘Gradualist’ Theory Which party prevails in Texas is a complicated
riddle. Historically a low-turnout state — it ranked second to last in the
2024 election, ahead of only Arkansas — Texas held a primary in March that
saw nearly one in four voters showing up to the polls, a modern record for
midterm participation, with Democrats slightly outpacing Republicans. A
few factors could conspire to thwart a blue wave in Texas. As of 2020,
straight-ticket voting is no longer possible in the state, which could
impact the mostly Democratic urban counties where that practice has
frequently been used by voters in past elections. Texas is one of only
eight states that lack universal online registration, while voting by mail
is also highly restricted. In January, Mr. Abbott turned over the state’s
list of approximately 18.7 million registered voters to the Trump
administration, and 1.2 million of them have subsequently been put on the
“suspense list” because their addresses have not been verified. The recent
shuttering of nearly one-third of Tarrant County’s polling sites by its
Republican-controlled county commission is particularly worrisome for
Democrats. “The reason we’ve lost these statewide races in the past is
because we’ve never gotten enough out of Tarrant County to overcome the
margins in rural Texas,” Ms. Davis said of the turnout. “If we don’t get
it to 53 or 54 percent this November, it’s game over. James and Gina can’t
win.” But the state’s Republicans have reasons of their own to be fretful.
Partly because of the recruitment efforts of the Texas Majority PAC and
Blueprint Texas, a down-ballot candidate support organization co-founded
by Ms. Davis earlier this year, the Democrats are fielding a full slate in
all 150 state races for the first time in a half-century. Though many of
these aspirants face long odds, their presence on the ballot could
energize the Democrats in predominantly conservative regions who have not
bothered to turn out in the past. “If we win on Nov. 3, most of those
names running down-ballot in really tough areas like East Texas and the
Hill Country and the Panhandle will be responsible,” Mr. O’Rourke said.

enthusiasm being sufficient to carry the day for Mr. Talarico, he also
doubted that a last-minute avalanche of negative ads would prove decisive
for Mr. Paxton. “At a certain point, there’s diminishing impact once you
get past an absurd level of spending,” he said. Rather than project a
winner in November, Mr. Henson said he felt more comfortable embracing a
“gradualist” theory, one in which Texas does not become blue overnight,
but instead competitive. “Even if Talarico loses by a Beto-like margin,”
he said, “the next cycle is a presidential election, where Trump likely
won’t be popular and Democratic turnout will be higher. So there are
reasons for Texas Democrats to be optimistic.”'

Save perhaps one. It is the idea, fantastical to many as it is irresistible to others, that the Democrats will win a statewide race in Texas for the first time in 32 years. According to the latest New York Times/Siena University poll of the race for U.S. Senate, James Talarico, a 37-year-old state legislator seen by national Democrats as one of the breakout stars of this cycle, is ahead of his Republican rival, Ken Paxton, the state’s scandal-plagued attorney general, by six points. The poll was conducted from Sept. 21 to Sept. 30. A survey from mid-September, the ReconMR/Siena Research Institute poll, also showed the Democratic gubernatorial candidate, Gina Hinojosa, four points ahead of the three-term G.O.P. incumbent, Greg Abbott, the most dominant political figure in Texas. Cue the fluttering heartbeats. Cue, as well, the eye-rolls. Given how thoroughly Republicans have dominated the state, and how the hopes of Democrats have repeatedly crashed, some Texas pollsters remain skeptical. “At some point, you do get conditioned by all that’s happened in the past,” said James Henson, the director of the University of Texas at Austin’s Texas Politics Project. “I mean, you look at the trends and you have to admit that something’s going on. But you still don’t want to believe your lying eyes, because you’ve been burned for so long.” Mr. Henson was referring to the perennial spectacle of much-ballyhooed Texas Democratic aspirants face-planting against the Lone Star State’s red wall. First came Tony Sanchez Jr., the swaggering and self-funding Laredo oilman whom Gov. Rick Perry dispatched in 2002 by an 18-point margin. Next was the state senator Wendy Davis, who attracted worldwide attention for her filibuster in the Texas Legislature against an anti-abortion measure but whom Mr. Abbott demolished by 20 points in 2014. Finally, the El Paso congressman Beto O’Rourke came up 2.6 points short of defeating Senator Ted Cruz in 2018 but then suffered a 10-point loss to Mr. Abbott four years later. Even with the awareness of such humiliations, Democrats find themselves maintaining that 2026 could, at long last, be the year. President Trump’s deep unpopularity and the prospect of a blue wave could, they insist, extend into the state he won by nearly 14 points in 2024. According to a September survey conducted by Texas Southern University, Mr. Trump is seven points underwater in Texas. Mr. Talarico has run an energetic and well-financed campaign, while Mr. Paxton has staged far fewer public events and has had to rely on outside groups to fund an attack-ad blitzkrieg against his Democratic opponent. The party’s demise there is not a product of ill fortune, Mr. Henson said. “Governor Abbott has built an impressive election machine that has benefited state-level Republicans again and again for a decade and a half,” he said. “And the Democratic machinery here is almost nonexistent.” A ‘Hollowing-Out’ I have written about the politics of my native state at regular intervals for more than three decades. After watching the Democrats’ century-long rule in Texas come to a decisive end with Gov. Ann Richards’s loss to George W. Its weaknesses are even more glaring farther down the hierarchy. In recent elections, as many as one-third of state races have gone uncontested by Democrats. One-fifth of the party’s county chairs and two-thirds of its precinct chairs have been left unfilled. Until last year, the state party had a negative operating budget. As the veteran Democratic consultant Matt Angle observed, “There’s been a hollowing-out of the party.” Still, those of us who recall the satisfied sense of invincibility among Texas Democrats after roughly a century of one-party rule have detected similar signs of overconfidence among the state’s ruling party. Mr. Paxton, a close ally of Mr. Trump’s, was impeached by the Republican-controlled State House (and later acquitted by the State Senate) in 2023 over allegations that included bribery. He was also accused by his wife of adultery. Mr. Trump endorsed him anyway, all but guaranteeing his landslide primary triumph over Mr. Cornyn but in the process testing the allegiance of center-right Texans. In similar fashion, the Texas G.O.P. is in danger of losing many Latino voters who voted for Mr. Trump in 2024 after years of siding with Democrats. “We adopted a lazy way of campaigning that bit us on the ass, and we’ve learned from that,” Mr. O’Rourke said. “Now it’s the Republicans who’ve gotten really lazy and complacent and comfortable.” Signs of Republican Overreach Simply spending one week driving through the vastness of Texas, as I did in September, is all it takes to appreciate an underdog party’s uphill battle. The state’s 32 million residents are spread across 20 media markets, many of them distinct ecosystems, from the urban colossi of Houston and the Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex to the oil patch of the Texas Panhandle to the Latino-dominated borderlands of the Rio Grande Valley. “When national donors are deciding where to invest, they look at a place like Iowa, where $5 million can fully fund a race,” said Katherine Fischer, the director of the Texas Majority PAC, which was established by the liberal philanthropist Soros family. “That’s why Texas is always at the bottom of their list. O'Keefe Defense Fund - Legal Update

Dear Patriot,

Early one morning in November 2021, FBI agents showed up at my home with a search warrant, and I asked to call my lawyer.

An agent handed me my phone and I unlocked it to make the call. Then he took it right out of my hand.

My name is James O'Keefe. I run O'Keefe Media Group, and for eighteen years I have sent undercover reporters into rooms that do not want a camera in them.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNDYsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAAA9ke_ETytxwOmpr9omUC8DUzD6Tzsj3_7QLJt9joYdo_YpGVsAJpnz2rXfqNIqbs4DSeFvnDci0ruR6mzi-M33JiEzQBSAgE33IkB2xX

For almost five years, the government's reasons for that raid were sealed. This year a federal judge ruled that the secrecy had gone too far, so the FBI's sworn affidavit is now public, and I have read every page of it.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNDYsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAAA9ke_ETzXZ3fXDuDOU4iJV31wPa39ukaeH9QXa3QdttKKsm2QRuDprIdeIssLO4MjwrtAaWk7vzJQberpnAeuXVFRPVyRypC_FFeEi6Z
CHIP IN $35 TO DEFEND JAMES →

The FBI already had my emails before it came to my door, because it had used search warrants to collect them from Microsoft.

That means agents read the email I sent my team on October 12, 2020, after a tipster brought us a diary that was said to belong to Joe Biden's daughter. In it, I told my team we would not publish the diary, because it was “indefensible to publish what we currently have.”

Nine days later I wrote to them again: “We can't publish this.”

The FBI quoted both of those emails in its own sworn affidavit, and more than a year later, it raided my home anyway.

The same agent swore that it “does not appear” my reporters “are, in fact, credentialed journalists.” Agents tracked my phone to a hotel upstate and planned to wait until I came home, and they even asked the judge for the power to press my fingers onto my phone and hold it up to my face to unlock it.

And after all of that, the government never charged me with a single crime. The judge said so in her own order: “no criminal charges were forthcoming.”

They never needed a conviction, because a raid works just as well if it costs a reporter years of lawyers, money, and focus. Liberty Guard runs the O'Keefe Defense Fund so that I can pay those lawyers and keep doing the reporting they wanted to stop.

| Friends,
How hard do you want your congressman to work? This seat belongs to you. It has been an honor to represent the best district in America for 22 months. My team and I have been on the ground building partnerships and solving problems for people across Virginia's 5th. We've walked into hundreds of businesses, many owners told me they'd never met their Congressman. I've attended 413 churches, tractor pulls, rodeos, visited hospitals, rural clinics, and more.
Yesterday we visited nine different county early voting locations encouraging folks to vote. Today we're visiting 9 more counties. We will start with the Hanover County precinct at 9am. Hope to see you soon.
Make a plan. Show up. If we show up, We Win.

Friend, it’s Congresswoman Ilhan Omar. I’m humbly, respectfully asking for just a minute of your time.
I’ve been under attack from Trump and all of MAGA since I first came to Congress in 2019.
He’s launched constant racist attacks at me and the Somali-American community. He’s said that he wants to “send me back.” He’s spread conspiracy theories and lies about my family and I. He called me “garbage.”
[](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/7?c0=io-em-dhs-oct26.4A7Axt&refcode=em261031-1-180&t=3&akid=2573%2E791427%2Eefkt5v)
But these personal attacks are nothing compared to what Trump did next.
After months of threatening to investigate me, revoke my citizenship, and deport me, Trump sent DHS agents to raid and search my home just weeks before the midterm elections in a clearly retaliatory, political stunt.
They took my phone, my documents, and revealed my home address to the people who consistently threaten my life. They subpoenaed my family and began a legal process that will take an immense amount of resources to fight.
Then, we got this bombshell report from _The Wall Street Journal:_
[](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/7?c0=io-em-dhs-oct26.4A7Axt&refcode=em261031-1-180&t=4&akid=2573%2E791427%2Eefkt5v)
**The Trump administration is looking to abuse its power to strip one of Trump’s loudest critics of their citizenship._It’s fascism._**
Trump’s goal is to intimidate and silence me, and by extension, this entire progressive movement and the immigrant communities we defend.
That’s because for the last two years, our movement has stood in steadfast solidarity with our neighbors in the face of ICE violence, MAGA corruption, billionaire domination, and a skyrocketing cost of living. We’ve fought back and won. Here in Minnesota, we showed the entire world just how weak and cowardly this administration really is.
Now, in just a few days, we have the opportunity to make our voices heard at the ballot box and sweep Trump’s corrupt sycophants out of power in Congress. We have to make the most of this moment.

Election Day is just three days away.
#
Hi there,
**Today is the last day to donate through Swing Left’s Immediate Impact Fund.**
With just three days to go, we want to ensure your donation reaches campaigns when they can still put it to work before Election Day.
Republicans have dropped hundreds of millions of dollars in these races to try to rescue their candidates, including over $400 million from Elon Musk alone.
That’s why we created the Immediate Impact Fund to ensure your dollars go exactly where they’re needed most right now. In this final stretch, the fund features 20 Democratic candidates in the House and Senate races that will impact the balance of power in Congress.

Over the next three days, your donations can help the candidates above turn out as many voters as possible—through boosted digital advertising budgets, last-minute voter contact to get supporters to the polls, and even hiring organizers to cure ballots if necessary.
Your donation will also power the Swing Left community’s work to turn out voters as we continue running Ground Truth canvasses and supporting campaign-run phone banks right up until polls close on Tuesday night.
The work we’ve done this year has been incredible to see—now let’s leave everything on the field and do everything we can over the next few days to help Democrats win.
Thank you,
The Swing Left Team
P.S. The races in our Reach Fund are looking closer than ever but need a last-minute boost. If you’re the kind of person who likes to take chances and wants to invest in tougher races, this fund is for you. Investing in these places now could win us an extra seat; if not, it builds groundwork that will make it easier for a Democrat to win next time.
