| | **_Meet Russell:_** Born and raised in Surfside Beach, SC, Congressman Russell Fry is the proud and homegrown Representative for South Carolina’s 7th Congressional District. Growing up in a cinder block home with no heating or air conditioning, Russell learned at an early age that hard work and perseverance pave the only true path to the American Dream. He watched his parents work day in and day out to make ends meet. And the values they instilled in him during his upbringing led Russell to self-fund both his undergraduate education at the University of South Carolina, and later his law studies at the Charleston School of Law. At Charleston, Russell served as the President of the Student Bar Association and even helped the school achieve its American Bar Association accreditation. He went on to practice law in the Grand Strand area for over a decade before entering the political arena to serve in the South Carolina House of Representatives for State House District 106 (Horry County). During his seven-year tenure in the SC House, Russell fought to safeguard Constitutional liberties, lower taxes, and put the best interests of South Carolina families above all else. He climbed the ranks to become Chief Majority Whip, and also chaired the House Opioid Prevention Study Committee. Under Russell’s leadership, 18 policy initiatives to combat the opioid crisis were signed into law. Since the first day he stepped foot in Washington, Russell has strived to shake up the corrupt status quo and deliver real change for the American people. He believes adamantly that so long as the American people stand united, we can keep the American Dream alive for every citizen of our great nation. Russell is a dedicated husband to his wife, Bronwen, and a loving father to his son, James. The family lives in Murrells Inlet with their chocolate lab, Jasper.

body:
Peter, With **Election Day just three days away** I've been thinking a lot about where this journey started.

I grew up in North St. Louis County, and this community has always been home to me. It's where I learned the importance of looking out for your neighbors, working hard, and standing up for what's right.

Those lessons have stayed with me throughout my life and my career in public service. From my time as a prosecutor to serving the people of St. Louis in Congress, I've always approached this work with one thing in mind: making life better for the people and communities that raised me.

And even now, after all the meetings, long days, and miles traveled on the campaign trail, that hasn't changed. Over the last few months, I've had the chance to talk with so many of you about what matters most to your families. Those conversations remind me why I got into public service in the first place.

Now, with just a few days left before Election Day, _I'm asking you to stick with me through the finish line._ Important work still lies ahead, and I'm grateful to have you by my side as we take these final steps together. body:
It may not seem like a lot, but it helps us have the resources we need in these last 3 days.
#
Peter,
**There are just 3 days left until one of the most important elections in a generation, and right now,_1.6 million Latino voters_ across Voto Latino’s 22 target districts still haven’t cast their ballots.**
These are new voters and voters who don’t always turn out. They’re registered, they’re eligible, and they’re reachable. Many of them just need a personal push from someone they trust to get to the polls.
And in these 22 districts, Latino voters will decide races that determine the balance of power in Congress. Our research shows that a shift of just a few thousand votes in any one of them could change everything.
Voto Latino has spent this entire cycle building the infrastructure, research, and relationships to reach exactly these voters. We know where to find them, how to talk to them, and which messages move them to vote. Now we’re putting all of it to work.
In the final days of an election, digital ads lose their punch, so every single dollar we raise from here on goes directly into the two most effective ways to reach voters right now.
1. **Text banking program:** Through our trained volunteers, Voto Latino will send one-on-one text messages to 200,000 new and infrequent Latino voters, sharing voting information and helping them make a plan for Election Day.

2. **Phonebanking operation:** Our bilingual volunteer will call voters across the country to answer questions, address concerns, and give voters the personal nudge they need to show up this November.

Today, we’re reaching out for your help: [**Will you chip in $1 right now to help us start reaching these voters today?**](https://act.votolatino.org/go/524?c0=em-ms-voto-20261031-2.fG7A7g&refcode=em20261031-745&t=1&akid=745%2E1366028%2E0F_KLL)
It may not seem like a lot. But when thousands of people across the country chip in $1 at the same time, it adds up fast, and it turns into texts sent, calls made, and voters reached in the places where this election will be decided.
These 1.6 million voters aren’t a statistic. They’re working families in the Rio Grande Valley, students in Phoenix, and small business owners in Las Vegas who have been targeted, threatened, and told their voice doesn’t matter. We have the plan and the people to reach them. _What we need is you._
**[Peter, will you chip in $1 right now to help us reach 1.6 million Latino voters before Election Day?](https://act.votolatino.org/go/524?c0=em-ms-voto-20261031-2.fG7A7g&refcode=em20261031-745&t=2&akid=745%2E1366028%2E0F_KLL)**
**[Donate $1 ››](https://act.votolatino.org/go/524?c0=em-ms-voto-20261031-2.fG7A7g&refcode=20261031-745&t=21&akid=745%2E1366028%2E0F_KLL)**
Thank you,
Voto Latino

Dear Patriot,

Early one morning in November 2021, FBI agents showed up at my home
with a search warrant, and I asked to call my lawyer.

An agent handed me my phone and I unlocked it to make the call. THEN
HE TOOK IT RIGHT OUT OF MY HAND.

My name is James O'Keefe. I run O'Keefe Media Group, and for eighteen
years I have sent undercover reporters into rooms that do not want a
camera in them.

[James O'Keefe on the FBI affidavit. Stand with James. Donate now.]
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

For almost five years, the government's reasons for that raid were
sealed. This year a federal judge ruled that the secrecy had gone too
far, so the FBI's sworn affidavit is now public, and I have read every
page of it.

CHIP IN $35 TO DEFEND JAMES →
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

THE FBI ALREADY HAD MY EMAILS before it came to my door, because it
had used search warrants to collect them from Microsoft.

That means agents read the email I sent my team on October 12, 2020,
after a tipster brought us a diary that was said to belong to Joe
Biden's daughter. In it, I told my team we would not publish the
diary, because it was “INDEFENSIBLE TO PUBLISH WHAT WE CURRENTLY
HAVE.”

Nine days later I wrote to them again: “WE CAN'T PUBLISH THIS.”

The FBI quoted both of those emails in its own sworn affidavit, and
more than a year later, it raided my home anyway.

DONATE NOW →
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

The same agent swore that it “does not appear” my reporters
“ARE, IN FACT, CREDENTIALED JOURNALISTS.” Agents tracked my phone
to a hotel upstate and planned to wait until I came home, and they
even asked the judge for the power to press my fingers onto my phone
and hold it up to my face to unlock it.

And after all of that, THE GOVERNMENT NEVER CHARGED ME WITH A SINGLE
CRIME. The judge said so in her own order: “no criminal charges were
forthcoming.”

They never needed a conviction, because a raid works just as well if
it costs a reporter years of lawyers, money, and focus. Liberty Guard
runs the O'Keefe Defense Fund so that I can pay those lawyers and keep
doing the reporting they wanted to stop.

GIVE WHAT YOU CAN TODAY →
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

Give today, and I will send you the key pages of the FBI affidavit
along with the judge's order.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.
I waived my own privacy rights so that these pages could be made
public, because I want you to see them.

Please give whatever you are able to give right now.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

In Truth,
[James O'Keefe]
JAMES O'KEEFE
Founder and CEO
O'Keefe Media Group

P.S. They read my emails. They saw me kill the story. They raided my
home anyway, and five years later, they have charged me with nothing.
That is what my lawyers are fighting, and I can't pay for it alone.

name: Jenny Beth Martin, Tea Party Patriots Citizens Fund
subject: The last weekend before Election Day. Are you in?
body:
Voters in key states are deciding now. One hour of texting this weekend reaches them.
Patriot–This is the last weekend before Election Day.In Georgia, Texas, and other states, early voting has now closed. For millions of voters, Tuesday, November 3, is the only day left to vote.Here is what worries me most. It is not the voters who disagree with us. It is the voters who agree with us and never quite get around to voting. They are not against us. They are busy. A text from a real person is often the reminder that gets them there.Tea Party Patriots Citizens Fund volunteers have now sent more than 700,000 text messages, on the way to goal of 1 million. Every one of them came from someone like you, on their own time, from home.**Here's what I need you to do today:**
1. Read [_**this simple instruction guide**_](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Ftpp-resources.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fdocuments%2FTPPCF-TextVoters-OnePager.pdf/1/010001a192216fa2-a830d96f-d241-43cd-9e08-1a79eadd608a-000000/ZT03AIEAyCvTXYvtIMjty3C5SHHcqQJoqK_s3xFKp7Y=452) to get started.

3. Set aside one hour on Saturday or Sunday and send texts to voters in key states and districts.

| Peter,
Louisiana is MAGA's death star. It is the place where they test their most insidious policies before firing them off at the rest of the country.
This summer alone, they canceled an ongoing election under a fake "state of emergency" and eliminated one of our majority-Black Democratic districts.
They passed a bill forcing homeless people into indentured servitude. They criminalized abortion. They deployed the National Guard into our streets. They tortured immigrants at the Winn Correctional Center in North Louisiana.
But a rebellion is brewing in the Bayou.
A catastrophic vulnerability has been found in MAGA's death star, and we are about to blow it wide open. Trump's approval rating in the state is underwater. Voters are fed up with the foreign wars, an economy on the brink of collapse, and National Guard and ICE storm troopers patrolling our own streets.
The rebellion has already struck. On May 16th, Democrats turned out in record numbers and delivered a blow that blindsided MAGA, sinking every single one of Governor Landry's amendments by 20 points or more.
Now a new poll shows Democrat Jamie Davis tied with MAGA candidate Julia Letlow in U.S. Senate race just 3 days before Election Day.

Peter, it’s Pat. In this election, there’s a lot we’re fighting against. Trump’s chaos. The GOP’s attacks on our freedoms. Prices that keep climbing while Washington looks the other way. But I believe we have to lead with what we’re fighting FOR. 250 years ago, our founders used the Declaration of Independence to make their case against King George. They also laid out what every person deserved: life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness. That promise is what still gives me goosebumps. Freedom for every American to make their own decisions about their lives and their bodies. A government that serves the people, not the powerful. Peter,

Most of what we send you is strategy: states, numbers, the plan to win. This one is about why we do this work at all. And that starts with Charlie Kirk.

Charlie launched Turning Point in the shadows of the Obama re-election campaign headquarters in Chicago. He was 18 years old.

Every established political force on the Left and the Right tried to stop him.

They failed.

What Charlie started grew into what is **the most influential activist organization in modern American history**.

We were privileged to work with him and be a part of this movement.

We joined Charlie because we believed our mission was the only viable way to save this country. Charlie was willing to do what nobody else in the conservative movement would do. He went looking for young Americans who cared enough about this country to act, and he gave them a reason to fight.

Then came 2020...

Under President Biden, we saw corruption, weaponization of the government, and a government promoting values that put Americans last.

Charlie was adamant that we do everything we could possibly do to fix this in 2024. **We DID IT** , and we must continue for 2026 and 2028 to have a shot at saving this country.

Now, it is on us to continue Charlie's vision and mission.

Every single day, we work to continue his legacy of recruiting, training, and mobilizing a new generation of citizens who love this country enough to do something about it.

That work does not stop at the campus gates. It's now changing the direction of the nation.

Right now, ballot chasers supported by Turning Point PAC are in the field in **states that will determine not just 2026, but the 2028 Presidential election**.

They are meeting voters face to face. They are building real relationships in these communities. They are chasing every ballot, whether it's cast on Election Day or by mail.

This is how we build the Red Wall.

Election Day is November 3rd.

name: United We Dream
subject: A scary thought…
body:
One signature away, and the clock is running. | | | Happy Halloween, Peter. 🎃 Want to know what scares us more than ghosts and monsters? **The thought of yet another congressional session ending without a vote on the Dream & Promise Act.** We’re ONE signature away from forcing a vote on a pathway to citizenship for millions of working people. Let’s make sure Congress can’t ghost us any longer. 👻 Timing is crucial. Congress has to be in session to collect signatures, so we only have between Nov. 9 and Nov. 12 to get the last signature. This is it: the final sprint. We are 3 days away from Election Day, and there will be no participation medal for this race. There’s no second chance at this, no slo-mo or rewind buttons. **We are within reach of victory, but we need every day, every door, and every dollar to get there. ** We have been running full speed for nearly a year, and we are seeing the results. After 200+ doctors and nurses endorsed us, a dozen current and former Republicans have launched Republicans for Perriello, helmed by former Rep. Denver Riggleman. _We are building a Coalition for Common Sense that is laser-focused on getting costs down, paychecks up and corruption out. _ Tens of thousands of local voters are turning away from the corruption, chaos and cruelty of this Congress, but that is not enough. We need to do the work to earn their faith that this campaign matters to them. That having me in Congress instead of John McGuire will meaningfully improve their lives. I know that is true, but I know that proving it takes work. **So let me just say this: I know that this campaign and coalition is ready to run through the tape. We are ready to keep running until we have delivered those results for our communities and our Constitution.** We don’t have an enthusiasm problem. We’ve got energy like I’ve never seen before, and a grassroots movement that spans every corner of the Fighting Fifth. _What we’re in danger of having is a resources problem._ With Cook Political Report and Fox News shifting the VA-05 race rating away from safely Republican, MAGA Inc. and outside groups are taking notice, and they are ready to flood our TV screens and mailboxes. We need to respond to every false flyer with facts. We need to respond to every attack ad with truth. We need to put fuel in the tank, literally, to keep reaching every fair, festival, and VFW hall. And we need to show the national party and donors how powerful the momentum here is. **I’m trying to raise another $20K these last few days, and while I wish I could talk to each and every one of you in person or on the phone, there are literally not enough hours in the day – so I’m asking you to help me out by contributing to this email.** **[Will you make a donation to my campaign right now?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142606080/657448541/1139833646?refcode=261031em_tp&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDQvMS84ODkyNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwMDFkZWY1ZS0zM2Q1LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=io-Dub-o87VdyWOJ9GUmqk1dHbTBnV-upruz_bBp6RQ=)** **[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-cgp-2026-perriello](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142606081/657448542/1139833646?refcode=261031em_tp&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDQvMS84ODkyNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwMDFkZWY1ZS0zM2Q1LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=io-Dub-o87VdyWOJ9GUmqk1dHbTBnV-upruz_bBp6RQ=)** I promise you my campaign team will put your support to good use with a historic GOTV program that works to turn out every voter we possibly can to flip this seat and deliver a courageous Democratic majority that the people of this Commonwealth and this country deserve. Thank you so much. –Tom

I’ve had a full month on the trail with Dr. Jermaine Johnson and Sam Skardon’s campaign for Governor and Lt. Governor. We rallied with Senator Warnock, Rep Jasmine Crockett, Senator Cory Booker, Senator Mark Kelly, Ambassador Rahm Emanuel and met thousands of voters across the state this month.
We also hosted our future Senator Annie Andrews in Lyman last week thanks to Mayor David Petty! We handed out thousands of voter guides across the state as well.
The best part by far was the people of South Carolina. We have so much possibility this election cycle, and it will all comes down to voter turnout. A historic number of early voters could close with a record 1 million turnout today. And a razor thin race for US Senate, the opportunity to break the supermajority in the state house and the chance to elect a Democratic Governor is all with in reach.
Democracy is a participatory sport y’all, and we’ve got less than 4 days. Stay with me!

**NYT/Siena Poll - October 2026**
**Annie Andrews (D): 48%**
**Darline Graham (R): 48%**
Winning here would be game over for Republicans’ majority. Let’s make it happen:
**[Will you split a $3 donation between Annie Andrews’ campaign and Chris Murphy’s mobilization fund? Every dollar goes a long way in a state like South Carolina.](https://act.chrismurphy.com/go/380?c0=csm-em-andrews.TwvkDJ&refcode=csm_em261031-90&t=1&akid=2849%2E1711221%2Er4sx4k)**
We’ve got a lot of races on the map this year, and a lot of them look close.

Annie is the kind of leader we need more of in the U.S. Senate. But we need to help her get across the finish line with a win first.

I’ve got a very important request for you this weekend:
**Please go vote!**
Don’t wait to make your voice heard — do it today! [**Vote centers are open now across California.**](https://act.alex-padilla.com/go/947?t=1&akid=1942%2E159979%2EiVrKNo)

So, check this off your list this weekend. And once you’re done, speak to your family and friends and make sure they vote too. There is simply too much at stake in these midterms to just sit by and not participate.

Alex Padilla

Because tonight, on Halloween, something truly terrifying is creeping toward South Carolina.

It isn't a ghost. It isn't a ghoul. **It's Annie Andrews, and she's been feeding on $25 MILLION in liberal cash to grow stronger.**

[Pledge your support](https://substack..7ct165lU1HUXEHGNuiTaVTzlBVmJs8ZFPRTztOgpOpg?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=222925251)
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=1454853&post_id=222925251&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjIyOTI1MjUxLCJpYXQiOjE3OTM0NTc5NDAsImV4cCI6MTc5NjA0OTk0MCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTE0NTQ4NTMiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.3FJM1cY9HtsULGL3wDwcuY3ixpGQ47ElBNfxDIWDe6Q)
Forget the ghosts, goblins, witches, and haunted houses.
**Want a real scare? Open your health insurance bill.**
Your premium went up. Your deductible got bigger. Your copay increased. And somehow, despite paying thousands of dollars for health insurance, you're still paying out of pocket when you actually need medical care.
Then comes the next Halloween surprise.
Your longtime doctor is no longer in your network. Your insurance company demands prior authorization. Or you're directed into a major hospital network for something that could have been handled in an independent physician's office.
And sometimes, you discover an additional hospital facility fee on your bill.
**You 're paying more for healthcare and getting less freedom to choose your care.**
That's not a Halloween trick. That's the frightening reality facing too many Connecticut families.
And unlike Halloween, the horror doesn't end November 1.
## The Hospital Network Monster
As a physician, I've watched healthcare change dramatically.
Independent medical practices have increasingly been absorbed into large hospital systems and corporate networks.
What used to be a straightforward visit to your local doctor can now involve centralized scheduling, insurance restrictions, facility fees, and layers of administration.
**Why should a routine office visit cost more simply because a hospital system owns the practice?**
Hospitals play an essential role in providing emergency and complex medical care. But not every patient needs a hospital, and not every medical service belongs in a hospital network.
Independent physicians, community practices, and outpatient facilities are essential to competition, accessibility, and affordability.
When large systems dominate healthcare markets, patients can lose choices and face higher prices.
**Healthcare should be organized around patients --not the financial interests of hospital corporations and insurance companies.**
## The Deductible That Keeps Getting Bigger
Here's another frightening trick.
You pay your health insurance premium every month.
But when you need an MRI, a specialist, a procedure, or even routine treatment, you discover you haven't met your deductible.
So you pay again. .... And again.
**At what point does health insurance stop feeling like protection and start feeling like another expensive monthly bill?**
Families can spend thousands of dollars annually on premiums while still facing substantial out-of-pocket costs.
And when patients delay necessary treatment because they cannot afford it, manageable medical conditions can become serious and expensive emergencies.
That's bad medicine and bad economics.
Insurance should protect families from financial catastrophe--not leave them afraid to use their coverage.
## The Hidden Halloween Trick: Your Employer Pays, But Your Paycheck May Suffer
Some Connecticut workers are fortunate enough to have employers who pay most--or even all--of their health insurance premiums.
You may not feel the full pain when the insurance bill arrives.
**But don 't be fooled. You may still be paying for it through a paycheck that isn't growing.**
When healthcare premiums increase, employers have to find the money somewhere.
And for many businesses, particularly small and midsize employers, healthcare is one of their largest employee benefit expenses.
That money could otherwise help fund higher salaries, bonuses, new jobs, or investments in growing the business.
Instead, more of the employer's compensation budget goes toward insurance and healthcare costs.
**Your employer 's healthcare bill goes up. Your salary stays flat. And you wonder why you're working harder but getting nowhere.**
This is one of the hidden costs of America's healthcare system.
And it's not just employees who suffer.
Small-business owners face difficult choices: absorb higher premiums, pass costs along to customers, reduce benefits, limit hiring, or hold back wage increases.
As a physician and attorney, I understand that this is more than a healthcare problem.
**It 's a wage problem. A jobs problem. And an affordability problem.**
Even if someone else pays your insurance premium, that doesn't mean healthcare inflation isn't costing you money.
**The scariest healthcare bill may be the one you never see --because you're paying for it in raises you never receive.**
That's why lowering healthcare costs isn't just about making medical treatment more affordable.
It's about freeing up money for better wages, more jobs, stronger businesses, and greater economic opportunity throughout Connecticut.
## Washington Has Had 18 Years. Where's the Cure?
My opponent, Congressman Jim Himes, has represented Connecticut's 4th District for 18 years.
During that time, healthcare has remained one of the most serious financial concerns for American families.
The Affordable Care Act expanded insurance coverage and established important protections. But having an insurance card is not the same as having affordable healthcare.
**If you can 't afford your deductible, can't see the doctor you choose, or can't understand your medical bill, the system still needs fixing.**
I've written about the need for change in my previous articles, including _[Hollywood Jim Deserves an Emmy](https://substack.com/redirect/e5e2ad3d-5452-44e4-8150-1820825bfd4e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ and my broader discussion of _[The Battle for Connecticut](https://substack.com/redirect/dd42310d-323b-427a-b0e2-a667180fea72?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_.
Healthcare is not an isolated problem.
It's part of a larger affordability crisis affecting housing, electricity, transportation, employment, and the ability of families to build a future in Connecticut.
And after 18 years in Washington, I believe it's fair to ask our congressman:
**Where are the results?**
I don't want another speech about how complicated healthcare is.
I want solutions.
## A Doctor's Prescription for Washington
I'm running for Congress because I bring something Washington desperately needs: medical experience, legal training, and practical problem-solving.
As a physician, I understand the challenges patients and doctors face when seeking and delivering care.
As an attorney, I understand how regulations, insurance contracts, corporate consolidation, and federal laws shape the system.
And as a father, I understand how rising costs threaten the next generation's opportunities.
**Here is what I will fight for in Congress:**
**1\. Restore competition and independent medical practices.**
Patients should have meaningful choices beyond the largest hospital systems. We need policies that support independent physicians, community practices, and competition.
**2\. Challenge excessive hospital facility fees.**
The same routine medical service should not automatically cost substantially more simply because it is performed in a hospital-owned setting. Greater price transparency and sensible payment reform can help.
**3\. Reduce premiums, deductibles, and out-of-pocket costs.**
Healthcare reform should be judged by what patients actually pay, not just by the number of people holding insurance cards.
**4\. Cut unnecessary insurance bureaucracy.**
Doctors should spend more time treating patients and less time fighting prior authorizations, claim denials, and administrative obstacles.
**5\. Put prevention before crisis.**
Early diagnosis, preventive care, and better access to physicians can improve outcomes and help avoid costly medical emergencies.
**6\. Protect families from catastrophic medical costs.**
Serious illness should not destroy a family's financial future. Health insurance should provide meaningful protection when patients need it most.
**7\. Make healthcare savings benefit workers and employers.**
Rising employer insurance costs can crowd out wage increases, hiring, and investment. We need to reduce the underlying cost of healthcare so businesses have more room to grow and reward their employees.
**My goal is simple: More healthcare. Less bureaucracy. Lower costs. Greater patient choice.**
## Connecticut Can't Afford Another Two Years of the Same Prescription
Healthcare isn't the only frightening bill Connecticut families face.
Our electricity bills are too high. Housing is increasingly unaffordable. I-95 has become a parking lot. Our trains are aging. And too many young people wonder whether they can afford to remain in Connecticut.
But healthcare is particularly personal.
When your child is sick, you shouldn't have to wonder whether the specialist is in your network.
When your parent needs treatment, you shouldn't have to fight an insurance company for authorization.
When you visit your doctor, you shouldn't be surprised by a hospital facility fee simply because the practice changed ownership.
And when your employer tells you there isn't enough money for a raise, you shouldn't have to wonder how much of that money disappeared into rising insurance premiums.
**We need a healthcare system that treats patients --not one that treats patients like revenue streams.**
As I've discussed in my other articles on [the Goldstein Substack](https://substack.com/redirect/dd42310d-323b-427a-b0e2-a667180fea72?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Connecticut needs leadership focused on solving these interconnected problems rather than producing more political theater.
## Connecticut Deserves a Second Opinion
When a patient isn't getting better, a good doctor doesn't keep prescribing the same treatment indefinitely.
* We reassess the diagnosis.
* We examine the evidence.
* We change the treatment.
* And we measure the results.

Washington needs that same approach.
**Jim Himes has had 18 years. Connecticut deserves a second opinion.**
I'm not running to become another television personality or Washington insider.
I'm running to bring medical judgment, legal experience, and practical problem-solving to Congress.
And this Halloween, my message is simple:
**NO MORE TRICKS FROM WASHINGTON.**
**IT 'S TIME TO PUT A DOCTOR IN THE HOUSE.**
* * *
## More From Dr. Michael Goldstein
If you want to understand why I'm running and what I intend to change in Washington, read more of my articles:

clean_body: The Real Halloween Horror: Rising Health Insurance Premiums, Bigger Deductibles, Hospital Networks, and the Raises You May Never Receive. | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more The Goldstein Substack - A Father-Son Publication Dr. Goldstein is Running for Congress and his page can be found The Real Halloween Horror: Rising Health Insurance Premiums, Bigger Deductibles, Hospital Networks, and the Raises You May Never Receive. | | | Oct 31 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- Happy Halloween, Connecticut! Forget the ghosts, goblins, witches, and haunted houses. Want a real scare? Open your health insurance bill. Your premium went up. Your deductible got bigger. Your copay increased. And somehow, despite paying thousands of dollars for health insurance, you're still paying out of pocket when you actually need medical care. Then comes the next Halloween surprise. Your longtime doctor is no longer in your network. Your insurance company demands prior authorization. Or you're directed into a major hospital network for something that could have been handled in an independent physician's office. And sometimes, you discover an additional hospital facility fee on your bill. You 're paying more for healthcare and getting less freedom to choose your care. That's not a Halloween trick. That's the frightening reality facing too many Connecticut families. And unlike Halloween, the horror doesn't end November 1. The Hospital Network Monster As a physician, I've watched healthcare change dramatically. Independent medical practices have increasingly been absorbed into large hospital systems and corporate networks. What used to be a straightforward visit to your local doctor can now involve centralized scheduling, insurance restrictions, facility fees, and layers of administration. Why should a routine office visit cost more simply because a hospital system owns the practice? Hospitals play an essential role in providing emergency and complex medical care. But not every patient needs a hospital, and not every medical service belongs in a hospital network. Independent physicians, community practices, and outpatient facilities are essential to competition, accessibility, and affordability. When large systems dominate healthcare markets, patients can lose choices and face higher prices. Healthcare should be organized around patients --not the financial interests of hospital corporations and insurance companies. The Deductible That Keeps Getting Bigger Here's another frightening trick. You pay your health insurance premium every month. But when you need an MRI, a specialist, a procedure, or even routine treatment, you discover you haven't met your deductible. So you pay again. .... And again. At what point does health insurance stop feeling like protection and start feeling like another expensive monthly bill? Families can spend thousands of dollars annually on premiums while still facing substantial out-of-pocket costs. And when patients delay necessary treatment because they cannot afford it, manageable medical conditions can become serious and expensive emergencies. That's bad medicine and bad economics. Insurance should protect families from financial catastrophe--not leave them afraid to use their coverage. The Hidden Halloween Trick: Your Employer Pays, But Your Paycheck May Suffer Some Connecticut workers are fortunate enough to have employers who pay most--or even all--of their health insurance premiums. You may not feel the full pain when the insurance bill arrives. But don 't be fooled. You may still be paying for it through a paycheck that isn't growing. When healthcare premiums increase, employers have to find the money somewhere. And for many businesses, particularly small and midsize employers, healthcare is one of their largest employee benefit expenses. That money could otherwise help fund higher salaries, bonuses, new jobs, or investments in growing the business. Instead, more of the employer's compensation budget goes toward insurance and healthcare costs. Your employer 's healthcare bill goes up. Your salary stays flat. And you wonder why you're working harder but getting nowhere. This is one of the hidden costs of America's healthcare system. And it's not just employees who suffer. Small-business owners face difficult choices: absorb higher premiums, pass costs along to customers, reduce benefits, limit hiring, or hold back wage increases. As a physician and attorney, I understand that this is more than a healthcare problem. It 's a wage problem. A jobs problem. And an affordability problem. Even if someone else pays your insurance premium, that doesn't mean healthcare inflation isn't costing you money. The scariest healthcare bill may be the one you never see --because you're paying for it in raises you never receive. That's why lowering healthcare costs isn't just about making medical treatment more affordable. It's about freeing up money for better wages, more jobs, stronger businesses, and greater economic opportunity throughout Connecticut. Washington Has Had 18 Years. Where's the Cure? My opponent, Congressman Jim Himes, has represented Connecticut's 4th District for 18 years. During that time, healthcare has remained one of the most serious financial concerns for American families. The Affordable Care Act expanded insurance coverage and established important protections. But having an insurance card is not the same as having affordable healthcare. If you can 't afford your deductible, can't see the doctor you choose, or can't understand your medical bill, the system still needs fixing. I've written about the need for change in my previous articles, including and my broader discussion of . Healthcare is not an isolated problem. It's part of a larger affordability crisis affecting housing, electricity, transportation, employment, and the ability of families to build a future in Connecticut. And after 18 years in Washington, I believe it's fair to ask our congressman: Where are the results? I don't want another speech about how complicated healthcare is. I want solutions. A Doctor's Prescription for Washington I'm running for Congress because I bring something Washington desperately needs: medical experience, legal training, and practical problem-solving. As a physician, I understand the challenges patients and doctors face when seeking and delivering care. As an attorney, I understand how regulations, insurance contracts, corporate consolidation, and federal laws shape the system. And as a father, I understand how rising costs threaten the next generation's opportunities. Here is what I will fight for in Congress: 1\. Restore competition and independent medical practices. Patients should have meaningful choices beyond the largest hospital systems. We need policies that support independent physicians, community practices, and competition. 2\. Challenge excessive hospital facility fees. The same routine medical service should not automatically cost substantially more simply because it is performed in a hospital-owned setting. Greater price transparency and sensible payment reform can help. 3\. Reduce premiums, deductibles, and out-of-pocket costs. Healthcare reform should be judged by what patients actually pay, not just by the number of people holding insurance cards. 4\. Cut unnecessary insurance bureaucracy. Doctors should spend more time treating patients and less time fighting prior authorizations, claim denials, and administrative obstacles. 5\. Put prevention before crisis. Early diagnosis, preventive care, and better access to physicians can improve outcomes and help avoid costly medical emergencies. 6\. Protect families from catastrophic medical costs. Serious illness should not destroy a family's financial future. Health insurance should provide meaningful protection when patients need it most. 7\. Make healthcare savings benefit workers and employers. Rising employer insurance costs can crowd out wage increases, hiring, and investment. We need to reduce the underlying cost of healthcare so businesses have more room to grow and reward their employees. My goal is simple: More healthcare. Less bureaucracy. Lower costs. Greater patient choice. Connecticut Can't Afford Another Two Years of the Same Prescription Healthcare isn't the only frightening bill Connecticut families face. Our electricity bills are too high. Housing is increasingly unaffordable. I-95 has become a parking lot. Our trains are aging. And too many young people wonder whether they can afford to remain in Connecticut. But healthcare is particularly personal. When your child is sick, you shouldn't have to wonder whether the specialist is in your network. When your parent needs treatment, you shouldn't have to fight an insurance company for authorization. When you visit your doctor, you shouldn't be surprised by a hospital facility fee simply because the practice changed ownership. And when your employer tells you there isn't enough money for a raise, you shouldn't have to wonder how much of that money disappeared into rising insurance premiums. We need a healthcare system that treats patients --not one that treats patients like revenue streams. As I've discussed in my other articles on , Connecticut needs leadership focused on solving these interconnected problems rather than producing more political theater. Connecticut Deserves a Second Opinion When a patient isn't getting better, a good doctor doesn't keep prescribing the same treatment indefinitely. We reassess the diagnosis. We examine the evidence. We change the treatment. And we measure the results. Washington needs that same approach. Jim Himes has had 18 years. Connecticut deserves a second opinion. I'm not running to become another television personality or Washington insider. I'm running to bring medical judgment, legal experience, and practical problem-solving to Congress. And this Halloween, my message is simple: NO MORE TRICKS FROM WASHINGTON. IT 'S TIME TO PUT A DOCTOR IN THE HOUSE. We’re officially lowering our ask.
Our average donation is typically around $27. Over the last couple of weeks, that average gift has dropped down to $22. Our supporters are giving less, and they’re giving less frequently. That’s a problem, and we get it.
10-4. Message received.
So, we’re only asking for $2 donations to this email. We’re lowering our ask. And we’re doing it for two reasons.

But second, we’re hoping that people chip in more than $2 if they can afford to do so. Covering down for the people who can’t give that $10 or $25.

name: Aaron's iPhone
subject: Good morning and happy Halloween, folks!
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the Committee to Elect Aaron Ford
body:
Good morning, folks, and happy Halloween!
I’m pumped for today. This morning, we’re kicking off our final get-out-the-vote push.
Our team and volunteers will be knocking on doors, calling voters, and making sure folks across Nevada hear from us before November 3rd.
The latest polling shows that whoever wins over these last-minute voters will likely win this whole thing — so it’s incredibly important that we get our message out to as many Nevadans as possible.
If you can, pitch in $5 this morning to fuel our final weekend of voter outreach. **Every door we knock on, and every call we make could be the one that clinches this race.**
**[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_af_20261031_1_ak](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_af_20261031_1_ak.D-b9Ol&amount=5&refcode=em20261031-1228&t=2&akid=1239%2E127862%2Ev8wceI)**
Thanks so much,
Aaron
Sent from my iPhone
Make a plan to vote on or before November 3! [**Click here for resources ››**](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/225?t=3&akid=1239%2E127862%2Ev8wceI)

This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Email is the most important way we keep in touch with people like you, so thank you for reading to the end.
To contribute via check, please make it payable to the "Committee to Elect Aaron Ford" and mail it to PO Box 96003, Las Vegas, NV 89193.

Peter,

You know what tricks the Democrats are trying to play on us this Halloween?

No treats. Just tricks. **[And every single one of them is designed to undo everything we've worked for.](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=392fc1a247fa41bb81bb06dfa1124296&_e=KSqeL3TeqUoqFc6TDnqDm15e081u97XgnoOUwkNNOkyeW2SbKzS2bUcXw5kgNf7NGxLKh68EpFz4KHFGy4gyi9xJQNtPCEsYzAeUVTebGusJn2-GTcgYF4MRIStZoVEs2-A8TmQNtmnmHnP-GJrs3nN1DBDsJ4o3_YRf4Qy8VJKnIesvy16NFuuiYHiS9buNqigLoh-90b3pjBHWfqqXGo06p8GN8SAq3EjgtuDcMRy55PgLYqFRfixScdbloIxAwAsoIW9x-nB8EDxQGYpia96M3TX6tJJQaXuMUlOgOUvBzey9Un3oFl6K2sXsuuRCB1k5XTvBiX-8rO6wQjkCy2ipf6KXvIaejvl3VaUYSq65GftI5EVqPIvDK3zC_DMv74rpEG63jXZqbfKZ5CGSO8CX6Rh0t_GcYfRA-8dYLwQCu4fUhZuAj5jmET7Xfjm9KXBhvoGXeOzrpgS8_RozWAYYAaJTLkkQIG_upjlxCgpXZ0DanBEeo4eBr0Op3ziqTwDuGW2cxPfa3eVEmesAfyuMSmWtFf3KSO9KPvhcWw2a_g1tQaMKOuphHpEPnVEHjqYXLXMlPOofbEHcXns7YPV_z9qB_0q56gFa0rLHeT8LQ7kTTqIxmaxje6a-TUPyPzsX4UeZ5i0Uo7nSv6QJvRBkoIoRf9hPBUSEgsutHUxUrUiF2B9s-FmCtEaz3Ju5qtDs0oEc9OMZlAN1LyG4kbZ64dLSTkBpVgDwV_2H-WdpZOHu5yWAPrELjLNddnwI-g4FuWA3mdy7i76zKszgF0-CpW6Bq3UM7RXPtc7L4_IRsyHZ4fBKWWfGGZ9pPeFJ6f_AhNS0q27bakNC1uUJgkwpA9QG3jDQH_s5oIlE-3x5rssMAkZGT7fn-NXJ4l2JQJBMnRl9VimGCb1Elrje104uE1fVFRZfAgjF_C3NFhuYyknbrsY_TycLNAmARZ8eVqfmFrSN1AAT40MB1wNGWUbWzme9VSWFPla46wH-CHHX_p8w5cpsgG3of7trURjQbPtlglgLvDm26YDEzFPHCfwsiR0ZSytVTZc0tFSTKOlV8CKaReWvLvln7DHIyHry)**

****Trick #2: Socialism, dressed up as "fairness."**** Higher taxes, government control, and a Democratic Socialist agenda creeping further into the mainstream every single day.

****Trick #3: Packing the courts, dressed up as "reform."**** Undoing decades of conservative judicial wins with the stroke of a pen.

****Trick #4: A Schumer-controlled Senate, dressed up as "checks and balances."**** In reality, it's the end of everything Republicans have fought for since 2024.

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: Facebook just took away two of our biggest tools.
body:
Here’s what Meta’s final-week ad blackout means for us.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter, I have bad news, and this one’s a little wonky, so bear with me.
**As of last Tuesday, our campaign can’t launch a single new ad on Facebook or Instagram.**
**[Before I explain what that means, will you chip in $5 right now to help us fill the gap?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261031_2_meta.IrmCrx&refcode=em20261031-2596&amount=5&t=2&akid=2596%2E299639%2EnSO38l)**
Here’s what you need to know: Every election cycle, Meta blocks all new political ads for the final week of the race. **That hits our campaign in two big ways.**
**First, we can’t launch new ads to win over voters.** Whatever ads Greg Abbott already had running can keep running. But through Election Day, we can’t put out a new ad answering his attacks. We can’t respond to breaking news in this race. And we can’t adjust our message on the platforms where millions of Texans spend their time.
**Second, we can’t launch new ads to raise money.** Facebook and Instagram ads asking supporters to chip in are a real part of how we fund this campaign. This month alone, they’ve brought in more than 10% of our online fundraising. Now, right when every dollar matters most, that tool is mostly off the table.
**That means two things have to happen this week.**
**_We have to take our message everywhere Meta can’t stop us:_** streaming TV and YouTube, digital ads on news sites and apps, and TV spots in the markets where this race will be won or lost.
**_And we have to pay for it with grassroots donations from emails like this one**_ , because email is now one of the most important fundraising tools we have left. Every dollar we raise this week goes straight into putting our message in front of the voters who will decide this race.
**[So I’m turning to you, Peter. What we raise from this email will help decide how much ground we can cover this week. Will you chip in $5 or any amount right now to help us keep our message in front of voters through Election Day?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261031_2_meta.IrmCrx&refcode=em20261031-2596&amount=5&t=3&akid=2596%2E299639%2EnSO38l)**

Thank you,
Gina

name: Anika Page
subject: Join us in Jackson for a conversation with Lord Andrew Roberts
body:
Join us in Jackson for a conversation with Lord Andrew Roberts | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/mspolicy/andrewrobertsevent-12855290?e=5703353baa)
---
|
---
| | Good afternoon Friend,
What can Winston Churchill’s life teach us about leadership, courage, and the challenges of our own time? We hope you’ll join the Mississippi Center for Public Policy on **Monday, November 16** , as we welcome acclaimed historian and author **Lord Andrew Roberts** to Jackson for a special luncheon and conversation. Lord Roberts is the author of _Churchill: Walking with Destiny_ , the acclaimed biography of Sir Winston Churchill. Drawing on previously unavailable material, including the wartime diaries of King George VI, his book offers a compelling look at the life and leadership of one of history’s most consequential figures. During our luncheon, Lord Roberts will share insights from his career studying history’s leaders and defining moments. It promises to be an engaging conversation for anyone interested in Churchill, history, and the lessons we can carry into the future.

In 1939, American Lutheran congregations passed a plate to rescue Europeans fleeing Hitler. The charity they built spent eighty years collecting nickels, quilts, and hymns. Today it's called Global Refuge -- rebranded from Lutheran Immigration and Refugee Service (LIRS) in 2024 -- and it collects something else entirely: federal appropriations. According to USAspending.gov, roughly $1.34 billion in federal transactions have flowed to this organization since fiscal 2020.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b0912c44-d013-41ae-87ef-1210781ebca6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Look at the shape of that money. From $67 million to a $340 million peak -- a fivefold climb, nearly a million dollars a day at the top. Then the turn: $230 million, then half that. Two presidents, two business cycles. This wasn't donors getting generous. This was policy.
**Two businesses**
Global Refuge runs two businesses out of Baltimore...

body:
That’s not democracy. That’s a purchase order.

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=3074%2E4032634%2EuWDCGj)
---
As of this message, Elon Musk has poured $446 million into these midterm elections — and that’s only the money that’s been disclosed so far. Nearly half a billion dollars (and counting) to help Republicans win. Think about that: the world's first trillionaire — the richest man on Earth — is trying to buy his own government. And why has he done that? Because he’s scared. Elon knows that a Democratic Congress could mean no more tax breaks for billionaires while working families struggle to get by. No more government contracts immediately coming his way. No more loose AI “regulations.” No more dumping millions of dollars into one election to get his way. A Democratic Congress would mean more accountability. And Elon knows that with Democrats in power, he will be held accountable, so he’s trying to buy himself a Congress that won’t ask questions. That’s not democracy. That’s a purchase order. It’s an investment he’s expecting a return on. **Elon Musk has his money. But what we have is the many. A grassroots movement — including you — of people who are sick and tired of our government working great for people like Elon Musk.** On Tuesday, it's voters — not Elon Musk — who will decide the election. Who will determine whether our government answers to working people or the billionaires trying to buy their own government. Elon understands the power of his money, but he’s underestimating the power of people who organize, show up, and make their voices heard. So please, take today and reach out to your friends and family about their plan to vote tomorrow, if they haven’t voted early already. Sign up to knock on doors or make calls to voters tonight, tomorrow, or Tuesday, if you can. Let’s use every minute we have left to counteract his hundreds of millions and show him that the many will defeat the money. name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: Odysseus
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Warren for Senate
body:
There may or may not be a picture of Bailey in his Halloween costume at the end of this email

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=3075%2E4032634%2EvV8CgZ)
---
No tricks, NO donation ask. Just a quick note from me (and a Halloween treat at the bottom). I know the flood of emails and texts asking for money is exhausting — and that times are tough right now for so many. I want to be direct and say that I never expect you to be able to respond to each message with a donation — and we’re grateful to have you on this team no matter how much or how often you’re able to donate. Chipping in with a donation is just one way to get involved. It’s important that we do what we can — donate, make calls, put up yard signs, put out messages on social media — because we’re so close in so many races. I’ve kept it up because I’m trying to help — and I know you are too. Take the email I sent two days ago for Abdul El-Sayed: The amount of billionaire-backed Republican PAC money pouring into Michigan to try and defeat him is mind-blowing. The contributions to that email can help keep his ads on television, where he can respond directly to those attacks in this closing week of his race. It can help make sure his field organizers have gas money. It can ensure there’s coffee in the pot and cookies on the table when volunteers get back from door knocking. And it will help build strong teams for elections to come. This team has supported candidates like him across the country: Angie Nixon, Mary Pelota, James Talarico, Juliana Stratton, Peggy Flanagan, Sherrod Brown, Troy Jackson. Good people whose races are on a knife’s edge. Good people who may win or lose based on a handful of votes. And whether they win or lose will have a lot to do with where our nation goes next. On whether we can hold Trump and his administration accountable for their corruption and self-dealing. On whether we can make child care affordable for every family, make the ultrawealthy pay their fair share through a wealth tax, and put real guardrails on AI so giant tech companies can’t put profits ahead of working people. On whether our democracy survives. I don’t want to wake up on the day after the election and talk about the good people who lost by just a bit — and say I wish I’d done a little bit more. And I don’t just want us to win. I want us to win BIG. Big enough that nobody can dismiss the results. Big enough to send a clear message that this country is ready to go in a different direction. So I’m giving it everything I’ve got. I’m grateful for everything that every one of you has already done. And I’m grateful for the chance to be in this fight with you. Happy Halloween, and thanks for being a part of this, Elizabeth P.S. Now here’s a treat: Bailey, a.k.a. Odysseus on his journey home, hopes you’re having a happy and safe Halloween!

---

Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country.

Since the Supreme Court gutted key provisions in the Voting Rights Act, extreme politicians have taken advantage to pass harsh laws that restrict access to the ballot box. These restrictions particularly affect disadvantaged communities and people of color. **Toplines for the Week**
The midterm story that's been building all year remains clear: this _should_ be an overwhelming victory for Democrats, and therefore for all Americans who oppose Trump. As I showed in last week's _Midterm HQ_ , we're poised for strong outcomes among state legislatures, governors, and the U.S. House, while the Senate is looking as good as could be hoped but still rests on a knife's edge. The newest numbers confirm it, though they've also added some important factors that I'll describe below.
But if you take away nothing else from this final pre-election _Midterm HQ_ or anything you read this weekend, I hope you'll hold on to this: **we need to be prepared for this fight to go well past November 3.**
It gives me no pleasure to write that. In fact, I hope I'm wrong.

name: NEGOP
subject: Reminder: 🚨 Your Weekly Update From The NEGOP
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the Nebraska Republican Party 1610 N St
body:
News, events, and action items to keep Nebraska red and growing strong.
| | | | |
---
| A message from Governor Jim Pillen...
---
| Fellow Republicans,
All eyes are on us as we head to the polls on Tuesday.
We have massive opportunity to stand together and defend our values and send a message to the far-left that they just don't get Nebraska. Let's tell them: Nebraskans believe in smaller government, lower taxes, and commonsense conservative solutions to strengthen the future of our state.
Between today and Election Day, keep talking to your family, friends, and neighbors. We all need to do our part to stand up for our values.
In Nebraska, only 26% of registered voters voted in the primary. Low turnout puts all the progress we've made over the last three decades at risk.
Write down the names of the people you will talk to about voting. Then make those conversations happen. You don't need a perfect speech. Make a call, send a text, or have a conversation after church. Tell them why you're voting, encourage them to make their voices heard, and ask them to make a plan to vote. From every corner of this state -- all 93 counties, rural and urban -- it is an honor to serve as your Governor.
We're running for re-election with the same priorities I committed to four years ago: kids, taxes, agriculture, values.
My promise to Nebraskans is that I'm the candidate who will fight to increase affordability, protect water/agriculture, strengthen our workforce, invest in our kids, and defend Nebraska values - protecting life, keeping boys out of girls' sports, and keeping our communities safe.
This is the season of democracy -- and this election is too important to stay on the sidelines. Vote for Republicans -- up and down the ballot. We have just a couple more days to make a difference that will last for generations.
Suzanne and I cannot thank you enough for everything you do for this state and the Republican party. We look forward to serving you for four more years.
Vote November 3rd!
Jim Pillen
---
| Letter from the Chair...
---
| Friends,
First, let's remember why we are voting. As Republicans our core principles center around love of God, country and family. Our votes safeguard those principles. We are in a tough battle, but I am confident that the good common sense of Nebraska voters will prevail. Time is drawing close to see if all of our hard work has paid off.
Four days. That's it. Democrats are throwing everything they have at Nebraska this year. Out-of-state money is flooding our airwaves, paid organizers are knocking doors in towns they've ignored for decades, and they are counting on one thing: that Republicans will think this race is already won and stay home. They are wrong, but only if we prove it. This is not the week to let our foot off the gas. This is the week we floor it.
If you have a mail ballot sitting on your kitchen counter, fill it out today. Do not put it in the mail this late. Drop it off at your county election office or an official drop box so it is in their hands before polls close on Tuesday. A ballot that arrives late doesn't count, no matter how you voted, and we cannot afford to leave a single Republican vote sitting in a sorting facility on November 4.
If you haven't voted yet, in-person early voting is open at your county election office through Monday, November 2. Or head to your polling place on Tuesday, November 3. Bring your photo ID. Then take someone with you. Call your spouse, your kids, your neighbors, and that friend from church who always means to vote but never quite gets around to it. Ask them when they're going, and offer to drive.
The Democrats are all in. So are we. Four days. Foot on the gas. Let's bring it home!
Together we win!
In Liberty and in Truth,
Mary Jane Truemper Chairman, Nebraska Republican Party

name: Rashida Tlaib
subject: Trump is out of control
body:
We’re not backing down in the fight against fascism. | | |
---
Friend, Donald Trump is weaponizing the federal government against our communities — attacking immigrants, intimidating voters, and using federal agencies to try to change the outcome of next week’s elections. That means **we need to not just win on Election Day, but win big.** Along with a strong number of progressive candidates, my sister-in-service Rep. Ilhan Omar and I are running for re-election right now. After the Department of Homeland Security recently raided Ilhan’s family home, Trump explicitly said that he wants to deport her, even though she’s a naturalized citizen. | | From conversations with local food providers about growing demand for assistance to fighting for good-paying jobs and lower prescription drug costs, October has been a month focused on the issues that matter to people across Northwest Washington. I want to share some of that work with you. Earlier this month, I met with local food banks, hunger-prevention organizations, and community leaders at the Lynnwood Neighborhood Center to discuss growing demand for food assistance. Families are struggling with higher grocery prices, and Republicans' cuts to SNAP will only make matters worse. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142619977/657490165/1596212816?refcode=2026-10-31-october&recurring=&amount=7&amounts=10,30,50,100,200&refcode2=91c1b803-43d5-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY1OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5MWMxYjgwMy00M2Q1LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=wmywpWPiip5YTHSPMqLsLdu6WClcUk6EShOSxnDn2_0=) In the past few months, my office has received dozens of messages from constituents worried about how they are going to afford prescription medications if the Trump administration's new rule goes into effect. I joined my colleagues in urging the Trump administration to delay a new rule that could make it harder for Americans to get affordable prescriptions from Canada and other countries. The administration announced a delay, and I will continue fighting to keep health care affordable. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142619978/657490166/-2067985552?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY1OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5MWMxYjgwMy00M2Q1LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=wmywpWPiip5YTHSPMqLsLdu6WClcUk6EShOSxnDn2_0=&emci=da8b6dd0-3fd2-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbd50&emdi=91c1b803-43d5-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&ceid=9494239) I also heard from farmers across Northwest Washington about how rising costs, including sky-high gas prices from the Iran War, are making it hard for them to make ends meet. I will keep fighting to end Trump's unjustified war and bring down costs. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142619979/657490167/1596212816?refcode=2026-10-31-october&recurring=&amount=7&amounts=10,30,50,100,200&refcode2=91c1b803-43d5-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY1OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5MWMxYjgwMy00M2Q1LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=wmywpWPiip5YTHSPMqLsLdu6WClcUk6EShOSxnDn2_0=) I also joined Senator Patty Murray in pressing the Trump administration to move forward with stalled border station modernization projects in Sumas and Lynden. Good news and bad news, Peter. **The good news** is that it looks like next Tuesday is legitimately going to be a strong night for Democrats. We are watching in real time as Republicans give up on tough battleground districts, pulling out money and redirecting it to places they think are “winnable.” **That brings us to the bad news.** *WE* are where that “winnable” money goes. When Republicans give up on other districts, they reinvest that money here. In NY-17. To support Mike Lawler. That means that we’ve seen a mountain of last minute spending flood into this district over the last week or so. We were already being outspent. Now, we’re in the fight of our lives with less than 72 hours until polls close. Cait can still win. We just need to keep our foot on the gas for this final sprint. As we speak, our team is knocking on doors across the district to take advantage of the last weekend of early voting. We have big plans for tomorrow, and are planning for an absolutely massive ground game on Tuesday. But if we’re going to be able to stand up against the last minute money AND power this type of on the ground outreach, we’re really counting on your support. [We’re respectfully asking you to donate $10 or even $17 to help elect Cait Conley. | | **IN CASE YOU MISSED IT: ** **‘Phil Scott is Far & Away the Best Choice’** _St. Albans Messenger Endorses Phil Scott for Governor_ On Friday, the _St. Albans Messenger_ endorsed Phil Scott as he seeks a historic sixth term as Governor of Vermont. [Read the full article here:](https://us.list-manage.com/SMEvyc936xH?e=19cebfe173&c2id=84d1094b3a168b6495ef78aca9f3540c) The article highlights Governor Scott’s fiscal restraint, moderate leadership and experience - all strengths Vermont needs right now with the instability in Washington D.C. and an increasing partisanship from the majority in the Vermont Legislature. “Mr. Scott has the necessary experience and is far and away the best choice to navigate Vermont for the next two years. He is a political moderate and long on experience.” The choice in the November 3rd election is clear. Amanda Janoo “is long on theoretical advice and woefully short of the experience Vermont needs in its next governor.” The Messenger emphasized how Janoo’s ideology diverges from reality in Vermont and why Vermont needs Governor Scott’s sensible leadership:
* “The new taxes [Janoo proposes] would make our marginal tax rate the highest in the nation. She contends it would generate over $320 million, but the amount hasn’t been verified. And paying for the state’s universal primary care needs would cost roughly $600 million. **Where does the extra $300 million come from?** ”
* “[Ms. Janoo] describes our tourist economy in Vermont as ‘extractive,’ which means she thinks we lose more than we gain. Really. **We attract about 16 million visitors each year, and they spend over $4 billion in our businesses.** That generates over $300 million in tax revenue.”
* “And, Janoo said she would limit the number of residents and businesses moving to Vermont to address our housing costs...Vermont is currently losing people and businesses. How do we stay viable if we continue to lose what we have? **How would she decide who is worthy of moving to Vermont? Has any state set up such a policy? Doesn’t that smack of discrimination?** ”

Luckily, Vermonters have a choice in this election. They can reelect **Governor Scott who has proven leadership and viable plans to address Vermont’s single biggest issue: Affordability**. Because**the real change** is tackling the affordability crisis one-party rule has brought to Vermont. -Team Scott ###

Hey folks,
Republican Congressman Thomas Massie is going scorched-earth on Donald Trump's own party, and he's not holding back. From the Epstein files to Pete Hegseth's potential impeachment to Trump's war in Iran, Massie is exposing some serious cracks inside the GOP just days before the midterms.
And here's the thing: I don't agree with Massie on much. But when someone is willing to stand up to corruption in their own party, we need to talk about it.
Here's what we get into:
* [**00:00:29**] Thomas Massie breaks with Trump over the Epstein files and the Justice Department's failure to hold powerful people accountable.
* [**00:02:03**] Massie predicts a better-than-50% chance of impeaching Pete Hegseth as Republicans prepare for a chaotic lame-duck session.
* [**00:04:28**] Why Massie's brutal criticism of Washington's political establishment reveals something bigger about corruption and accountability.
* [**00:07:24**] Netanyahu's election fraud claims, Elon Musk's Ukraine controversy, and the growing backlash against Trump's war in Iran.
* [**00:10:46**] The GOP's staggering hypocrisy and why building a massive, cross-party coalition could be essential to protecting the midterm elections.

This isn't about suddenly agreeing with Thomas Massie on everything. It's about recognizing that Donald Trump's grip on the Republican Party is showing real signs of weakness, and that people across the political spectrum are fed up with corruption, reckless wars, and politicians putting themselves ahead of the American people. ### **Help us beat and replace the mainstream media! Support PolitiBrawl by becoming a paid subscriber today:**
[ Support Our Journalism](https://substack.com/redirect/4f70c1e2-9041-4c55-ad76-91eb9c36f61f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
A few weeks ago, the nation was gripped with the news of a Homecoming football game in Minneapolis' suburbs being interrupted by gunfire. The shooting not only resulted in the game being canceled, but it forced the Homecoming dance to be canceled.
It did not take long for people to find out the people involved in the shooting were part of the metropolitan region's Somali gangs. Reports indicate a fight broke out in a parking lot next to the football game when the suspected shooter got out of a car and fired into the melee, hitting two people.
The suspect is 18-year-old Adam Abdihakeem Adam. He is being charged with assault and riot with a dangerous weapon. Despite being charged in a serious and nearly deadly incident, **[Fox 9 reported](https://substack.com/redirect/76ad3554-e749-40cb-94c1-06e14901afd9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Adam was released on pre-trial bail after he posted a $100,000 bond, or a cash bond of $10,000.
In addition to the car used in the shooting being on camera, police found Adam in possession of the same clothes on the suspect in the surveillance footage.
New court documents allege the fallout from the shooting at Eden Prairie's football game did not stop that night. Another **[shooting that took place in nearby Bloomington](https://substack.com/redirect/ab15cd0f-89d7-498c-bfbe-29b76a94b4f2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** was in retaliation for shootings in Eden Prairie and other areas of the Twin Cities.
**PolitiBrawl is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support our work, please consider becoming a paid subscriber.**
[ Upgrade to paid](https://substack..MXDnBzvCq_edwoqWMwXZ21gIk8q7Yxc0lpbz_j_fYBQ?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=220917266)
Around 100 rounds were fired in the Bloomington incident, with one minor injury.
Police say Abdirahman Ahmed Jama, who was the target for the Bloomington barrage, had filmed himself "numerous videos that showed him in possession of numerous firearms (pistols, rifles, etc.) over the preceding months."
Police further said that Jama is seen in the videos "handling firearms in a reckless manner which is a threat to public safety."
It never seems to end for Minneapolis-St. Paul. Law enforcement across the area are having to contend with brutal gangs that have little regard for human life or consequences for their actions. What makes it worse is that the immigration policies championed by soft-hearted Midwesterners and the federal government are responsible for making the state more like Mogadishu.
At a certain point, some people have to be okay with admitting that _maybe_ it was not such a good idea to import such a culture into the Midwest. Not that I think that side will admit to such a thing, because their beliefs won't let them, which will only result in more of these incidents happening.
How this ends is anyone's guess. It seems the Twin Cities would benefit from more support by federal law enforcement because local resources are unable to keep up with the gang war, clearly. Even when they have the prime suspect in custody, local progressive policies prefer to have him back on the street, which not only endangers him but other people who could be caught in a 100-round crossfire.

Peter, Being from the Valley means everything to me. As our campaign draws to an end in a few days, it’s been on my mind more than ever. To be from the Valley is to make this country run. We’re the farmworkers who get up at the crack of dawn to feed the rest of the country, even when so many of our own families struggle to feed themselves. We’re the oil and gas workers who keep the lights on for people all across America. To be from the Valley is to work hard every single day, to support your family and your neighbors. But no matter how hard we work, so many of us are still struggling just to get by. And that’s why I decided to run. For far too long, we’ve been represented by politicians who care more about power than people, and who have been more interested in catering to corporations than fighting for the families who actually live here. I’ve always believed that if you want to represent a community, you should have the respect to show up for it -- not only on the campaign trail but every single day after you’re elected. And with three days left until Election Day, there is still time to restore that promise and elect someone who understands what it means to be from the Valley. **[There’s still time to make an impact, Peter. Before you head out for trick-or-treating tonight, I wanted to jot one last note about what we're so close to accomplishing in a few short days, and I hope you'll take a minute to read this all the way through.
**What 's at stake in this midterm election?**
I know I don't have to tell you: Right now, families are watching prices rise faster than their paychecks. Healthcare, groceries, and housing eat up more of the monthly budget every month. Meanwhile, our servicemembers are caught up in another conflict in the Middle East that's still driving up gas prices with no end in sight. I know when I talk to folks across Nevada, I hear the same thing again and again: People just want a government working on real problems. And winning back the Senate majority is the first step.
**What happens in the Senate matters for the country.**
Being in the Senate, I know how much a Democratic majority matters. Decisions that shape the lives - and pocketbooks - of everyday Americans are made or blocked in the Senate. The Senate has a say in who leads the Pentagon and who sits on the Supreme Court for decades. It controls which bills ever get a vote and which fall to the cutting room floor.
Right now, too much of the Senate's power is squandered, as the GOP majority just rubber stamps Trump's destructive agenda. A Democratic Senate would reclaim that power and get back to work for Americans like you.
**Here 's where we stand, 3 days out:**
The voices of the media and pundits have gotten louder in recent weeks, making the case that Democrats can do this. We've seen good polls - but we can't get complacent. We're only going to win back the Senate by fighting as hard as we can every hour we have left.
A blue Senate means Democrats have to hold all of our blue seats and then pick up four Republican-held seats from a field that includes Alaska, Iowa, Kansas, Maine, North Carolina, Ohio, and Texas. A year ago, even optimistic Democratic strategists wouldn't have guessed we'd have a real shot in some of these states that voted for Trump by double digits in 2024.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/95e669b1-6b92-477f-b16c-52618b5f9fc2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Source: 270toWin
It's important to note this shift didn't happen by accident. It happened because people like you showed up, volunteered, talked to their neighbors, and donated to fund campaigns that the experts said were long shots.
**So we have to keep our foot on the gas.**
Leading up to this final stretch, Republicans and their dark money allies are outspending Democrats in eight of the nine battleground Senate races to try to crush the grassroots momentum we're seeing in the polls.
🔴 In Ohio, Republicans are outspending Democrats by $29.8 million.
🔴 In Texas, Republicans are outspending Democrats by $26 million.
🔴 In Iowa, Republicans are outspending Democrats by $8.9 million.
The list goes on.
**Democrats don 't have this kind of big money support, but we don't need it.** We have something better: YOU. The Democratic edge has always come from our big team of people who care, coming together, and giving what they can.
I'm grateful for all of you who have been contributing to this team to help flip the Senate blue. The generosity of your time, money, and effort is making a HUGE difference. If you've been on the sidelines waiting for your moment, this is it. The moment is here.
Every dollar we raise between now and our end-of-month deadline at midnight - our final one before Election Day - will show Republicans that we have what it takes to overcome their big money donors, push our Democrats over the finish line on election night, and flip the Senate blue.
**[We don't have a moment to squander, so I have to ask - and this will be the last time I do before the election: Will you give what you can right now to help us in these final 3 days?](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/48bda2c7-66f1-4da6-83f5-f0ed10e72c14?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[Donate](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/48bda2c7-66f1-4da6-83f5-f0ed10e72c14?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
3 days. Let's make them count.
Jacky
* * *
##### `A personal note from Sen. Jacky Rosen:`
##### `My work in the Senate has always been defined by who I am and where I come from. Growing up as the granddaughter of immigrants and the daughter of a World War II veteran, my family instilled in me the values of hard work, determination, and persistence at a young age.`
##### `Now, I'm proud to fight tirelessly in the Senate to deliver progress for hardworking families like mine in Nevada and across our country. But with Donald Trump in the White House and Republicans in control of both houses of Congress, I need your grassroots support to keep up the fights that matter most.`
##### `Senate Democrats like me are the only thing standing in the way of Trump's extreme agenda that will hurt everyday Americans. That's why I need people like you on my side to help defend our progress and reclaim power from the GOP.`
##### `If you're with me, will you chip in now to help Democrats take back the Senate majority?`

| | | Thank God for Halloween candy, because the unsustainable intake of sugar – along with the profound gift of hope you keep providing – fuels me and my team through this final stretch. I know I’ve reached out a lot the last few days, but October’s end is nigh, and we are eager to be prepared for every possible trick. Our race is officially rated a toss-up – even CNBC was talking about it as _the race to watch on Election night_ – and MAGA and Musk money is flooding the district with attack ads. We are about to go from the northern to southern tip of this district to turn out supporters and fight back against misinformation, so I’m personally asking: will you contribute whatever you can to help fund our final GOTV push of the election? | I wish I had better news to share with you. **Unfortunately, I just got word that a new super PAC has entered our race.**

Since 1927, federal law has barred the U.S. Postal Service from delivering handguns through the mail.
#

Since 1927, federal law has barred the U.S. Postal Service from delivering handguns through the mail.
Donald Trump’s Justice Department has said it won’t enforce that law. The USPS has proposed rewriting its rules. And Lauren Boebert has introduced a bill to end the ban for good. No background check, no license, no training required to have a handgun shipped to someone’s door.
Whether that bill goes anywhere depends on one thing: Who controls Congress after Tuesday. A gun safety majority stops it. A gun lobby majority could pass it.
That’s the choice in front of voters in three days. GIFFORDS PAC is pushing to reach as many undecided voters as we possibly can, across the closest races in the country. Tonight at midnight is our last deadline to fund this final push.
