body:
I need you in my corner until the very end.
With Election Day just days away, I’ve been reflecting on why I got in this race.
I was guided by a simple principle: **When you love this country, you fight for the people who make it work.**
And yet, I’ve seen Ohioans working harder than ever and still being left behind while Washington politicians give handout after handout to billionaires and corporate special interests.

When we fought to save the pensions of tens of thousands of Ohio retirees, we stood up to Wall Street and _won._ When we fought to cap insulin prices and bring down the cost of prescription drugs, we stood up to Big Pharma and _won._
I knew a campaign founded on the idea of unrigging the system for working folks had the legs to win. This movement we’ve created has been truly incredible – and it’s all thanks to supporters like you.

name: Roy Cooper
subject: Not everyone will get this from me today
body:
Hey, Peter – I wanted to reach out directly.
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1689&source=&t=1&akid=5120%2E124072%2EWOfrHs) | | | |
---
Peter, not everyone will be getting this email.
I’m only reaching out to a select group of folks – people who haven’t donated to our campaign yet, but have stayed engaged with our updates and might be inclined to chip in for the first time today. **Your name was on that list.**
First, I want to say thank you for even opening this message. Your inbox is likely packed with emails like this right now, so I don’t take your time and attention for granted.
Here’s the deal: **The deadline to hit our final end-of-month fundraising goalbefore Election Day is at 11:59 p.m. tonight. To ensure we have the resources to reach every last voter between now and Nov. 3, I set an ambitious $5 million goal for our team to reach in the next few hours.**
Frankly, we’re running out of time to make our case to North Carolinians – and a recent poll of likely voters shows that 7% are still undecided.
If they all end up siding with my MAGA opponent because we let far-right super PACs have the final word on the airwaves, **our lead in this race could shrink overnight.** With Senate control at stake here, that’s a risk we simply cannot afford to take.
Unlike my opponent, Michael Whatley, this campaign is not bankrolled by billionaires. More than 95% of our donations last quarter were $100 or less, so when I say this movement is powered by small-dollar support from people like you, I mean it, Peter.
**That’s why I’m personally asking for your help today.[_Will you please chip in your first $5 donation to help us reach this ambitious goal by the midnight deadline? The results of this battleground race will shape the future of our country, so your support couldn’t come at a more urgent time._](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1689&amount=5&t=8&akid=5120%2E124072%2EWOfrHs)**

be overestimating Democrats' lead by several points.

Voters here are paying attention, and our volunteers have spent the last few weeks on doors from Westminster to Fullerton making sure they stay that way. **The bad news: Most of CA-45 still hasn’t voted.** Roughly 350k ballots are still sitting at home across the district. Every one of those ballots belongs to a voter we can still reach. That only happens if our volunteers have the walk lists, phone banks, and support they need to reach those voters by Tuesday. **[Tonight’s deadline is our last chance to fund that final push. clean_body: Turnout is up. Here’s what keeps us up at night. | = Folks, happy Halloween! 🎃 = Derek’s ready for trick-or-treating (and three more days of doors) We’ll keep this quick. Today is also our end-of-month deadline, the last one before Election Day, so here’s where the race stands with three days to go. The good news: Turnout in CA-45 is running ahead of 2022. Voters here are paying attention, and our volunteers have spent the last few weeks on doors from Westminster to Fullerton making sure they stay that way. The bad news: Most of CA-45 still hasn’t voted. Roughly 350k ballots are still sitting at home across the district. After we won by 653 votes in 2024, Republicans made this seat one of their top targets – and these last three days are their final shot at it too. That’s the scary part. You’ve heard it before: we must take action because democracy is at risk.
Donald Trump and his Republican allies have tried to manipulate elections. They know the playbook: voter suppression, election denial, intimidation at the polls, and gerrymandering. Put them together, and we steadily lose the ability to control our own futures.
But we are not afraid. This is a moment to channel outrage into action. And that is exactly how the Fair Fight team defends democracy.
I founded Fair Fight to advance voting rights after the 2018 election. When I saw eligible voters facing inexcusable barriers, I refused to be silent. I knew we needed a new coalition of patriots who would insist that every eligible voter can register to vote, cast their ballot, and have that ballot count.
Since then, the Fair Fight team has fought to protect those pillars of free and fair elections.
And in the run-up to Tuesday’s elections, they’ve strategically invested in races that are vital for turning back the tide on rising autocracy.
They’re fighting to flip the Georgia State House from red to blue, which is finally within reach after years of laying the groundwork. And they're fighting to elect Southern Democracy Champions to Congress who’ve stood up to new gerrymanders this year — and will keep fighting for fair maps and voting rights in Washington.
But these elections are hotly contested, and there’s a real chance we could fall just short of crucial victories. If MAGA Republicans cling to power, they will try to make that power permanent through more voter suppression and map-rigging. This is a pivot point for democracy — it could go either way.
[I’m asking you to donate to Fair Fight today because it would make a meaningful difference to elect Democracy Champions and preserve our freedoms.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142626355/657513642/-1736262579?refcode=emm_ff_20261031_SYANOR_v1s3&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDMvMS84ODQ1MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3ZGZkMGRkZC00Y2Q1LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=UyCGcP6-BfErfXopUQpHcT3Ks08qPSNodKbSKqDQgPw=)

Stacey Abrams

| | Before anything else, I want to say thank you.

In September, I launched Because Women Can with a simple belief: qualified women deserve the resources, support, and political infrastructure to compete and win. I’ve spent my career in public service watching talented women get overlooked, underfunded, and told to wait their turn. Leadership is everywhere. Investment isn’t. I built Because Women Can to help close that gap.

You were among the very first to step up. This wave of early support is already helping us build a pipeline of women ready to lead at every level, from city hall to the U.S. Senate. I am deeply grateful.

Election Day is **Tuesday, November 3** , and I’m proud to share the first slate of women BWC PAC is standing behind:
* **Angie Nixon, U.S. Senate, Florida:** A grassroots organizer who won her primary despite being outspent about 32 to 1.
* **Deb Haaland, Governor of New Mexico:** Former Interior Secretary, running to become the first Native American woman elected governor of any state.
* **Emilia Sykes, U.S. House, Ohio’s 13th:** A proven winner in one of the country’s most competitive districts, fighting for Akron and Canton.
* **Shomari Figures, U.S. House, Alabama's 2nd:** A born and raised Alabama native fighting for better health care, agriculture policy, and youth enrichment.
* **Sam Forstag, U.S. House, Montana's 1st:** An American labor union leader and former smokejumper looking to represent Montana.

This week, please make your plan to vote, and forward this email to friends in Florida, New Mexico, Ohio, Alabama, and Montana. And if you haven’t already, **[you can donate anything you can to help us keep growing.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142627191/657516527/-1217081304?amount=25&source=EM_NBI_BWC_20261031_ST_Endorsement_0_3MO_BonnieWatsonColeman_NA_NA_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDY4NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlNzgzN2Y1Ni00ZWQ1LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=sQ2OMb8Y6bMHTCbqWLQOI931y_HRbq-UdW6UqORZKbE=)**

This is only the beginning. Thank you for being part of it.

Bonnie Watson Coleman

| | Happy Halloween, Peter! 🎃 We hope you’re having a spook-tacular GOTV weekend!

Here’s a quick reminder that **Election Day is Tuesday, November 3,** and everything you need to vote is in one place:
* **Polls are open** 7am to 8pm on Election Day
* **Already have your ballot?** Return it at an official ballot drop box or vote in person at a voting location. The Secretary of State recommends returning ballots by mail at least 7 days before Election Day, so with only 3 days left, a drop box or voting location is your best bet.
* **Want to vote early in person?** Check the options near you here: **_[https://caearlyvoting.sos.ca.gov/](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142627561/657517765/59522984?source=EM_NBI_MT_20261031_FR_GOTV_0_3MO_TeamThompson_NA_NA_1-3&refcode2=&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDYvMS84NDQ0OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlOGE0YTFiOC00ZmQ1LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=x8mFI148JHPLMno-kukEnUJLgtKK0xcj-R2UIUp5q3s=&emci=ea40222a-55d1-f111-bf5b-00224829f869&emdi=e8a4a1b8-4fd5-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&ceid=2678920)_**
* **Need your polling place?** **_[Find it here](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142627563/657517766/1697095066?source=EM_NBI_MT_20261031_FR_GOTV_0_3MO_TeamThompson_NA_NA_1-3&refcode2=&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDYvMS84NDQ0OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlOGE0YTFiOC00ZmQ1LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=x8mFI148JHPLMno-kukEnUJLgtKK0xcj-R2UIUp5q3s=&emci=ea40222a-55d1-f111-bf5b-00224829f869&emdi=e8a4a1b8-4fd5-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&ceid=2678920)_**
* **Want to review your ballot first?** The Official Voter Information Guide has candidates and propositions: **_[https://voterguide.sos.ca.gov/](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142627566/657517769/2080778256?source=EM_NBI_MT_20261031_FR_GOTV_0_3MO_TeamThompson_NA_NA_1-3&refcode2=&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDYvMS84NDQ0OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlOGE0YTFiOC00ZmQ1LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=x8mFI148JHPLMno-kukEnUJLgtKK0xcj-R2UIUp5q3s=&emci=ea40222a-55d1-f111-bf5b-00224829f869&emdi=e8a4a1b8-4fd5-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&ceid=2678920)_**

Once you’ve voted, please tell or text a friend, family member, or neighbor and ask if they have their plan. A reminder from someone they know can be what gets a ballot turned in, and another step closer to winning this thing once and for all.

Thank you for everything you’ve done to get us here.

Team Thompson

Folks,
Today is the last day to vote early in North Carolina! Polls close at 3 PM. After then, you'll have to wait for Election Day: Tuesday, November 3rd.
We are in the final three days of the campaign, and I'm traveling across the state talking with as many voters as I can before Election Day. So I'll keep it quick.
If you've already voted, thank you. Reach out to your friends, family and neighbors and help them make a plan to vote too.
If you haven't already voted, you have a couple final opportunities.
* Find your early voting location [here](https://substack.com/redirect/f668f967-2ae0-489a-942a-da26d955a0ed?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* Find your Election Day voting location [here](https://substack.com/redirect/bf7b8f4c-2759-43c4-8f7c-1474193e0b3e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

**And if you haven 't registered to vote yet, register and early vote today** -- you won't be able to register to vote on Election Day!
This is the final stretch of the campaign, and we're working hard to continue organizing all across the state before polls close on Tuesday.
If you're able to help us talk with voters in these last couple days, you can [volunteer here](https://substack.com/redirect/0fac26d3-5527-4deb-9678-10819b5f95db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). And if you [chip in $5 today,](https://substack.com/redirect/406dff07-3078-4fd8-b243-a62cc7c7b3af?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) every dollar goes towards helping reach voters in these final days.
[Volunteer](https://substack.com/redirect/0fac26d3-5527-4deb-9678-10819b5f95db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Donate now](https://substack.com/redirect/406dff07-3078-4fd8-b243-a62cc7c7b3af?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Let's finish strong.

Donald Trump’s administration: tariffs hiking the prices of everyday
goods, slashes to Medicare and Medicaid, and out-in-the-open corruption
and self-dealing while millions of Americans struggle to get by.

I was born and raised in Manchester, New Hampshire. I grew up working at
my family’s restaurant, where I learned the value of hard work,
accountability, and serving the community. These values guide everything I
do.

The Granite State shaped who I am, and it’s why I’ll never stop standing
up for our community and fighting back against Trump’s chaos.

That’s why they’ve poured an unprecedented amount of cash trying to buy
this seat. They want another rubber stamp for the Trump agenda, not a
fighter for New Hampshire values.

We can’t let them win. But if we’re going to
fight back against the millions being spent against us, I need your help
to reach our $2,000,000 end-of-month fundraising goal before midnight
tonight.

No amount of money can buy what the strength of this grassroots movement

your first
$5 to help us reach our goal? Every dollar goes directly
towards fueling our voter outreach during these final days so we can win
on November 3rd.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261031_5.TNWldo&amount=5&refcode=em20261031-5&t=1023&akid=9921%2E582294%2EE4zBzz ]Donate $5 »

Thank you for standing with me in this fight,

Chris

We can’t let Trump and MAGA Republicans maintain their trifecta.
#

I need your help to close the gap on our final end-of-month fundraising goal.
# [](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1&akid=9904%2E582294%2ELzw9DC)
This isn’t the kind of message I wanted to send you today.
With only a few hours left before our final end-of-month fundraising deadline of the election season, **we _still_ have a critical gap left in our $2,000,000 goal.**
**[Can I count on you to rush $5 or whatever you can afford right now before midnight tonight to help us close it?](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261031_3.vlyJ16&refcode=em20261031-3&t=2&akid=9904%2E582294%2ELzw9DC)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261031_3.vlyJ16&amount=5&refcode=em20261031-3&t=3&akid=9904%2E582294%2ELzw9DC)**
**I know $2,000,000 is an ambitious target**
But I also know what this team can accomplish when we come together. If everyone reading this email chips in what they can right now, we’ll close the gap and secure the resources we need to fuel our final three days to Election Day.
Make no mistake about what we’re up against: John Sununu and MAGA megadonors are spending millions of dollars trying to buy this Senate seat.
**The only way we can fight back is with grassroots supporters stepping up right now to help us reach our $2,000,000 goal.**
Keeping New Hampshire blue is critical for Democrats to flip the Senate this year, and our opponent knows it. If we don’t have the resources to compete, we’ll be drowned out during these crucial final days by Sununu and his dark money allies.
I refuse to let that happen, and I need your help to make sure it doesn’t.
That’s how we’ll win and how Democrats will flip the Senate.
**[So please, will you chip in $5 right now to close the gap on our fundraising goal before midnight tonight so we can hold the line and win?](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261031_3.vlyJ16&refcode=em20261031-3&t=4&akid=9904%2E582294%2ELzw9DC)**

Thank you,
Chris

Donald Trump has spent months spreading conspiracy theories about our elections and trying to interfere with the democratic process, refusing to rule out sending troops to polling places or blocking states from certifying results. We’re fighting his administration’s completely baseless lawsuit against California, and so far, we’re winning — because we have the facts and the law on our side. **With our fundamental right to vote under attack from a President hell-bent on interfering in our elections, exercising that right has never been more important.** Every eligible Californian has the right to vote — and as we enter the final days of this election, my office remains fully prepared to protect that right. Let me be absolutely clear: We will not allow Donald Trump to intimidate California voters or interfere with our elections. Across California, attorneys, investigators, and staff from my office are on call and ready to respond in real time to any threats to your right to vote. _If you can imagine it, we are prepared for it._ Donald Trump wants to sow doubt and confusion. He wants us to lose faith in our elections. We cannot and will not let his un-American and anti-democratic tactics win. And the best way to fight back is to make our voices heard at the ballot box. **If you haven't voted yet, take a minute right now and make a plan for how, when, and where you will vote. Drop off your ballot, or vote in person by 8:00 PM on Tuesday, November 3.**[**You can find dropbox locations, early voting locations, Election Day polling places, and ballot tracking information right here.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142628637/657520882/775848546?refcode=261031em_rb_gotv&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MTI2MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2ZTUzM2YyMC01M2Q1LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=MTfLKsKYIFliGVXyE9TNrL4yjGvJbLCaT3I2d6bMsS8=&emci=6d533f20-53d5-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&emdi=6e533f20-53d5-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&ceid=33430436) I'm proud to have cast my ballot because our democracy is worth showing up for. I hope you'll join me by voting on or before November 3. —Rob

My husband and I own an auto-repair shop, and I represent a district Trump won three times, which apparently makes me his favorite hobby. = Trump and his allies are cutting their losses in swing districts nationwide—pulling money out and moving on, but not here. Here, they’re doubling down. Trump has spent more than $8 million in this district, and the Speaker of the House has been here three times to fundraise and campaign with my opponent. Outside groups are on track to outspend us by $10 million because this race is tied, and whoever wins controls who decides the House. = = It is a stupid system, but somebody’s gotta break it, and I’d rather it be a whole lot of people throwing in $3 than one idiot billionaire with a checkbook. = Thank you, Marie Glusenkamp Perez = | | | | | ---|---|---|--- Congresswoman Marie Gluesenkamp Perez represents Washington’s 3rd Congressional District. I’ll be honest with you... this hurts.
**_I _poured_ my heart into my last message. But maybe I set my hopes too high, Friend. _**
I was _counting_ on people like you. I really thought we’d see a big show of support after my last message... but it just didn’t happen.
**And the truth is, as hard as it is to say, we can’t keep doing the hard work we set out to do without the support to keep going.**
I’m Katie Britt. I came to Washington to stand up for hardworking families like yours, __not to play politics or sit on the sidelines_._
They’re coming after me with everything they’ve got. They’ve _**lied**_**about me on TV** , _**twisted**_ **my words** , and made me one of their **_top_ Republican targets** all because they know I won’t back down and **_they’re _terrified_ of the fight I bring to the table._**
This isn’t easy for me to ask, but I mean it with _**everything**_ I’ve got:
**[Will you please chip in anything, even just a few dollars, to help us stay in this fight?](https://link.email.brittforsenate.)**

I’m ready to keep fighting for our _values_ , our _families_ , and our _country_.

\- Katie Britt (R-AL)

| | | Peter, 72 hours. That’s how long until the polls close on Election Day, and until we find out whether Trump gets two more years of free rein — **or a Congress that finally slams the brakes on his agenda.** Everything we’ve fought for this year comes down to what we do between now and then. And we’ve fought hard. Since January, you’ve helped our movement:
* Endorse **1,200+ candidates** on the ballot
* Host **1,500+ events** , from phone banks to canvasses
* Talk with**650,000+ voters**
* Find **250,000+** supporters ready to vote
* Make **30 MILLION+** calls, texts, and door knocks

Those 250,000 supporters are our margin of victory, but only if they actually vote. For the next 72 hours, our job is simple: get every last one of them to the polls, and reach _every_ voter we haven’t talked to yet. **Do you know what the other side is doing in that same 72 hours? Flooding every screen in the country with attack ads, and praying we get lazy.** That’s the whole Republican strategy: drown out the truth with billionaire money and wait for us to run out of steam. [**So let’s ruin it. name: Elaine Luria
subject: “repair the world”
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Elaine Luria for Congress
body:
It’s called tikkun olam.

---
| | There’s a Jewish concept I learned from my mother and grandmother long before I could spell it. It’s called _tikkun olam_. It means “repair the world.” It’s the obligation to leave things in better shape than you found them. # SATURDAY, OCTOBER 31, 2026
---
**A Note from Cole, CEO of _The Flyover_** Dear Reader, Every year, auditors count how many copies America's biggest newspapers actually put in people's hands. The new numbers are brutal. Of the 25 largest papers in the country, 24 shrank last year. Average decline: 12.5%. Nearly a quarter-million daily papers, gone in a single year. _The Denver Post_ now prints about 24,000 copies a day. _The Arizona Republic_ , 33,000. _The Houston Chronicle_ , 35,000. _The Dallas Morning News_ , under 40,000. These are metros of millions. And the steepest collapse in the country belonged to _The Washington Post_ : down 21% in a single year to fewer than 88,000 print copies. The industry will tell you it's the internet. It's a convenient story, because it means none of this is their fault. Here's the story they won't tell: Americans didn't stop caring about the news. They stopped trusting the people delivering it. Somewhere along the way, the papers stopped reporting what happened and started campaigning for what they wanted to happen--and their readers noticed. Trust in the media now sits at the lowest level ever recorded. So no, that's not an audience drifting away. That's a jury coming back with a verdict. And here's the part the industry really doesn't want to talk about: those readers didn't give up on news. They went looking for someone who would just tell them the truth. Millions of them found their way to _The Flyover_ --a morning news publication built on one simple deal: We call things what they are. We keep the spin out and trust you with the facts. And _The Flyover_ stays free. It turns out that when you just give people the facts and trust them to think for themselves, people respond. So today I'm asking: will you help us continue? If news that plays it straight is something you want to see thrive, will you stand behind us? Chip in and support the news that gives it to you straight and free, every morning. Will you make a generous donation to support _The Flyover_? While the biased legacy media is failing, will you join our movement to keep the bias out of the news, free to your inbox every morning? I'd be grateful if you did. clean_body: Every year, auditors count how many copies America's biggest newspapers actually put in people's hands. | | | | | SATURDAY, OCTOBER 31, 2026 A Note from Cole, CEO of The Flyover Dear Reader, Every year, auditors count how many copies America's biggest newspapers actually put in people's hands. The new numbers are brutal. Of the 25 largest papers in the country, 24 shrank last year. Average decline: 12.5%. Nearly a quarter-million daily papers, gone in a single year. The Denver Post now prints about 24,000 copies a day. The Arizona Republic , 33,000. The Houston Chronicle , 35,000. The Dallas Morning News , under 40,000. These are metros of millions. And the steepest collapse in the country belonged to The Washington Post : down 21% in a single year to fewer than 88,000 print copies. The industry will tell you it's the internet. It's a convenient story, because it means none of this is their fault. Here's the story they won't tell: Americans didn't stop caring about the news. They stopped trusting the people delivering it. Somewhere along the way, the papers stopped reporting what happened and started campaigning for what they wanted to happen--and their readers noticed. Trust in the media now sits at the lowest level ever recorded. So no, that's not an audience drifting away. That's a jury coming back with a verdict. And here's the part the industry really doesn't want to talk about: those readers didn't give up on news. They went looking for someone who would just tell them the truth. Millions of them found their way to The Flyover --a morning news publication built on one simple deal: We call things what they are. We keep the spin out and trust you with the facts. And The Flyover stays free. It turns out that when you just give people the facts and trust them to think for themselves, people respond. So today I'm asking: will you help us continue? If news that plays it straight is something you want to see thrive, will you stand behind us? Chip in and support the news that gives it to you straight and free, every morning. Will you make a generous donation to support The Flyover? While the biased legacy media is failing, will you join our movement to keep the bias out of the news, free to your inbox every morning? I'd be grateful if you did. Our promise: we answer to you. Help us keep it. -- Cole CEO, The Flyover | | The Flyover, LLC 1910 Thomes Ave. Cheyenne, WY 82001-3527 | ---|---

| I have to tell you, sending an email on Halloween is pretty low on my list of things I'd like to be doing tonight. Sending a fundraising email? Even lower.
But here we are, three days before Election Day, and tonight at midnight is our last fundraising deadline.
Unfortunately, that's the reality of running for Congress in a country where elections cost millions of dollars and wealthy donors have far too much influence over who gets elected.
It's also one of the things my fellow democratic socialists and I want to change.
We're fighting to get big money out of politics, strengthen campaign finance laws, and build a democracy where working people have just as much political power as the billionaires who can write six-figure checks without blinking.
I'd love to live in a world where candidates could spend less time asking people for money and more time talking with them about rent, health care, child care, and all the things Congress should actually be working on. But until we change the rules, campaigns like ours still have to raise money to pay for organizers, voter outreach, and everything else that goes into running for Congress.
[Tonight at midnight is our final fundraising deadline before Election Day. If you're able to chip in $10 before then, here's where you can contribute >>](https://irrem7hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001NgIVXlWkOfyhb_ErMpBlLCWpp-Ums5nBl0GReg6wFWh1tdLftTlIdlTdn97LuR4jljsW_LCLd5xtcBrnLt5-hq1HE27Eqvjksq0-r4Fu3GgXGe5PuGR_vTIB6qhs9n7HrOH1RSX3wZtQCpu8v9Gu4sT_CEdH-A-e-oSYV9gyCcMc44Jxs9Fa0NghzOemd2UwWJnZyqV8ZUIBRn8hr3-mufLZtXOnFNzmUWIRw0a5KACzY-Gyr5BYTTYMGCc-kiiy&c=iN2K6zMnH85oW9Kipyus0aHRsm6gYNiBM36AvBcgxpDDYa_DqA_KfQ==&ch=slBqozlqfNxFkVkw13JK-cfTFTys-io7Xd76fJAJeOovOxqRwXwm4w==)
And if you've already supported us this month, thank you. I hope you get to spend tonight doing something considerably more fun than reading campaign emails.
Eat some candy for me.

clean_body: Our last fundraising deadline before Election Day is midnight tonight | | | | | == | I have to tell you, sending an email on Halloween is pretty low on my list of things I'd like to be doing tonight. Sending a fundraising email? Even lower. But here we are, three days before Election Day, and tonight at midnight is our last fundraising deadline. Unfortunately, that's the reality of running for Congress in a country where elections cost millions of dollars and wealthy donors have far too much influence over who gets elected. It's also one of the things my fellow democratic socialists and I want to change. We're fighting to get big money out of politics, strengthen campaign finance laws, and build a democracy where working people have just as much political power as the billionaires who can write six-figure checks without blinking. I'd love to live in a world where candidates could spend less time asking people for money and more time talking with them about rent, health care, child care, and all the things Congress should actually be working on. But until we change the rules, campaigns like ours still have to raise money to pay for organizers, voter outreach, and everything else that goes into running for Congress. == And if you've already supported us this month, thank you. I hope you get to spend tonight doing something considerably more fun than reading campaign emails. Eat some candy for me. In solidarity forever, Claire | | == | People will power this campaign. October 31, 2026
Congressman Himes does not appear to be worried that Republican Mike Goldstein will unseat him in the upcoming election. He has run few if any advertisements and is sitting on $2,400,000 in his campaign coffer while Goldstein has $12,000.

Plus, Congressman Himes has been a good sport and agreed to two debates with Goldstein even though he didn't have to do so.

The problem for Congressman Himes is that Goldstein is both a doctor and lawyer and is highly intelligent and well-versed on the issues. Thus, in [the first debate, ](https://substack.com/redirect/193bddbc-3ff3-489e-bd55-8cafe1da45f8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)Congressman Himes was poorly prepared and Goldstein dominated the debate.

Himes, who is both Harvard educated and a Rhodes Scholar, was not about to let this happen again. Thus, in the second debate he came out swinging, attempting to tie Goldstein to Trump while blaming both for inflation, the Iran War and the Jets' losing season (Okay. I made the last one up).
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/188af7c8-d757-4963-93e0-0c6869d866c7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---

Goldstein simply responded that Himes has been the Congressman for Fairfield County for 18 years and blaming Trump for the district's high housing, health insurance and energy costs along with the endless traffic congestion was silly. He further pointed out that Himes can't even get the money to finish the Congress Street Bridge in Bridgeport - a project that has been going on for ten years.

What happened next was hilarious. When questioned on the issues by the Connecticut Examiner moderator - who was very fair - Himes morphed into a Republican.

He agreed with Dr. Goldstein that the reason more housing wasn't being built was because of bureaucratic requirements, totally oblivious to Goldstein's charge that the Democrats created this bureaucracy.

Unlike in the previous debate, where Himes was a champion of renewables to save the planet, Himes now conceded that fossil fuels were here to stay for the foreseeable future and that Democratic policies preventing the building of natural gas pipe lines in Connecticut to lower energy costs were wrong. He even endorsed using more nuclear power.

In his opening statement, Himes lambasted President Trump on his inflationary tariffs that the president supposedly initiated to protect American jobs. But when questioned on this issue, Goldstein used his experience as a doctor to point out that American patients are too dependent on medications manufactured by other countries and how this created a bottleneck during COVID. He furthermore pointed out that having computer chips and steel products manufactured in the United States were crucial to our defense.

Not only did Congressman Himes agree, he added that the loss of manufacturing jobs had devastated the economies in places like Youngstown, Ohio and Altoona, Pennsylvania.
Himes did his best to pummel President Trump for the Iran War, but when Goldstein pointed out that Iran was responsible for terrorist attacks throughout the world, Mid East instability and was led by feudal theocracy who discriminated against women and gays, Himes had little to say. Instead, he babbled incoherently about how the feckless Obama administration had stopped Iran's nuclear program and agreed to inspections - which is pure fiction.

But perhaps the most memorable part of the debate was when Goldstein dubbed the Congressman Hollywood Jim. Anyone who watched this debate could not help but notice Himes' movie star looks, and how he missed his calling. He could have played the villain chasing Leonardo DiCaprio in _The Titanic_ , rather than being a do-nothing Congressman.

He has run few if any advertisements and is sitting on $2,400,000 in his campaign coffer while Goldstein has $12,000. Plus, Congressman Himes has been a good sport and agreed to two debates with Goldstein even though he didn't have to do so. The problem for Congressman Himes is that Goldstein is both a doctor and lawyer and is highly intelligent and well-versed on the issues. Thus, in Himes was poorly prepared and Goldstein dominated the debate. Himes, who is both Harvard educated and a Rhodes Scholar, was not about to let this happen again. Thus, in the second debate he came out swinging, attempting to tie Goldstein to Trump while blaming both for inflation, the Iran War and the Jets' losing season (Okay. I made the last one up). | | ---|---|--- Goldstein simply responded that Himes has been the Congressman for Fairfield County for 18 years and blaming Trump for the district's high housing, health insurance and energy costs along with the endless traffic congestion was silly. He further pointed out that Himes can't even get the money to finish the Congress Street Bridge in Bridgeport - a project that has been going on for ten years. What happened next was hilarious. When questioned on the issues by the Connecticut Examiner moderator - who was very fair - Himes morphed into a Republican. He agreed with Dr. Goldstein that the reason more housing wasn't being built was because of bureaucratic requirements, totally oblivious to Goldstein's charge that the Democrats created this bureaucracy. Unlike in the previous debate, where Himes was a champion of renewables to save the planet, Himes now conceded that fossil fuels were here to stay for the foreseeable future and that Democratic policies preventing the building of natural gas pipe lines in Connecticut to lower energy costs were wrong. He even endorsed using more nuclear power. In his opening statement, Himes lambasted President Trump on his inflationary tariffs that the president supposedly initiated to protect American jobs. But when questioned on this issue, Goldstein used his experience as a doctor to point out that American patients are too dependent on medications manufactured by other countries and how this created a bottleneck during COVID. He furthermore pointed out that having computer chips and steel products manufactured in the United States were crucial to our defense. Not only did Congressman Himes agree, he added that the loss of manufacturing jobs had devastated the economies in places like Youngstown, Ohio and Altoona, Pennsylvania. Himes did his best to pummel President Trump for the Iran War, but when Goldstein pointed out that Iran was responsible for terrorist attacks throughout the world, Mid East instability and was led by feudal theocracy who discriminated against women and gays, Himes had little to say. Instead, he babbled incoherently about how the feckless Obama administration had stopped Iran's nuclear program and agreed to inspections - which is pure fiction. But perhaps the most memorable part of the debate was when Goldstein dubbed the Congressman Hollywood Jim. Anyone who watched this debate could not help but notice Himes' movie star looks, and how he missed his calling. He could have played the villain chasing Leonardo DiCaprio in The Titanic , rather than being a do-nothing Congressman. | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Joseph Bentivegna 541 Cromwell Avenue, Rocky Hill, CT 06067 ? ?

Today is Halloween.
And recent polls have MAGA's ghouls running scared all across the country, as an unprecedented blue tsunami chases in their wake:

However, there is one spine-chilling scenario for Democrats.
One where we take back the Senate and House....but quietly lose critical state Supreme Court races down ballot.
Michigan, Montana, and North Carolina all have state Supreme Court elections with massive implications:

* In Michigan, two liberal justices are fighting for their lives to stay on the court. A loss here would pave a path for MAGA to take back the court in coming years.

* In Montana, progressives are attempting to keep their majority on the court in what is considered a deep red state. If MAGA wins, the court flips.

* In North Carolina, Democrats are defending Justice Earls' seat. A win for Democrats here sets up an opportunity to flip the court entirely in 2028.

Losing these races would be so devastating that it could haunt the party for decades.
To make matters scarier, the high-profile Senate and House races are hogging the headlines and the endless TV ads, and these Supreme Court candidates might as well be ghosts.
That is where Defend Our Courts comes in. In the final, frightening days of this election, we are shining a flashlight into the dark corners of the ballot. We are putting a spotlight on these races and contacting Democratic voters so they know exactly who to vote for.
We have scared off MAGA's court takeovers before. In 2025, we spearheaded the defense of Pennsylvania's Supreme Court. With the help of over 100,000 Democrats nationwide, Pennsylvania's liberal justices kept their majority by landslide margins. We did it again in Wisconsin earlier this year and helped deliver another blowout that sent MAGA running for the exits.

| | Peter, In **1924** , Native Americans were finally recognized as U.S. citizens. In **1948** , New Mexico finally let Native people vote — recently enough that elders in Pueblo communities today were alive when their parents couldn't legally cast a ballot in their own homeland. In **2018** , the first two Native American women ever reached Congress. And on **Tuesday** , that century-long arc could finish: the first Native American women in the U.S. Senate. The first Indigenous woman governor in New Mexico itself. Five Indigenous women on one ballot, all primed to win. A hundred years of this story was carried by people who never got to see the ending. We are three days from it. The last stretch gets carried the way every stretch was — by people who decide it matters, right at the moment it matters most. clean_body: There are elders who remember when their parents couldn't vote There are elders who remember when their parents couldn't vote | ~~ | | Peter, In 1924 , Native Americans were finally recognized as U.S. citizens. In 1948 , New Mexico finally let Native people vote — recently enough that elders in Pueblo communities today were alive when their parents couldn't legally cast a ballot in their own homeland. In 2018 , the first two Native American women ever reached Congress. And on Tuesday , that century-long arc could finish: the first Native American women in the U.S. Senate. The first Indigenous woman governor in New Mexico itself. Five Indigenous women on one ballot, all primed to win. A hundred years of this story was carried by people who never got to see the ending. We are three days from it. The last stretch gets carried the way every stretch was — by people who decide it matters, right at the moment it matters most. ~ If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | ~~ Thank you. — Indigenous Women Lead | Paid for by Indigenous Women Lead PAC Indigenous Women Lead PACPO Box 15845Washington, DC 20003United States

Hey all, it's Charles here. My general consultant and chief strategist Kamauhas an important message to share with you directly, so I'll let him take it away:
* * *
It's Kamau, Charles' chief strategist. I want you to hear this from me directly:
This week, our campaign was the target of a cyberattack. Overseas hackers tried to break into the communication systems used by Charles and our campaign leadership, and they went after our website too. We've also learned they got into at least one staffer's Signal account sometime in the past couple of months.
The FBI and other law enforcement agencies are involved, and we've taken the steps needed to secure our campaign's systems and private data.
Here's how Charles put it:
"The fact that foreign actors attempted to hack and infiltrate our campaign systems so close to the election is only proof that we're in a position to win. Our enemies, both domestic and abroad, don't want to see this campaign succeed and are scared."
**He 's right. Nobody goes after a campaign they think is going to lose.**
But being in a position to win isn't the same as winning. Election Day is almost here, and the best answer to an attack like this is to show that this campaign is stronger than ever.
**Will you chip in right now to show them we won 't be intimidated, and help us continue our efforts to get out the vote?**
[Donate to Charles' campaign now](https://substack.com/redirect/7f3f8730-8442-4614-8694-7253547e0ad6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
These desperate tactics will not stop a campaign built by and for the people of Kentucky. The threats have been neutralized, and we're staying at full throttle all the way to Election Day.
Thank you for standing with us,
Kamau

Peter, Happy Halloween from Team Hunt! Tonight the scares are the fun type, and tomorrow morning the cobwebs come down. **I wish the same were true of Washington.** The House of Representatives is a haunted house in the oldest sense. Bad ideas are trapped there and never leave. Policies that failed forty years ago still rattle their chains in those halls. The place is possessed by special interests, and the extremist politicians doing their bidding survive on one trick. **They dress ordinary people up as monsters and tell you to be afraid. ** [**Chip in and help us end the extremist ghost stories for good.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqs6gc2C5hUDUAX_oNaSPVDobFeqfVfzIW2x4J26hzyt89u4WueHpNz587aG9m_9mASzx-UmnX3QKX5bUZET7YZcwmbaxG1B3gWApQblV4Vz1B4UFHGcBGH7TyE6cG-VnRmVEwSovtvmARthOF4H_ReaS8_Jiwl6DLCu3hNTL4yPMeypsHUyoNZxhUmXt0npKO4VtYOQ_hJ_N4tzd6BGdWLTFp0AT--BlX3AmrLxpVV5vjmhnuzjdEQWlr-OmT6w5T34neSilr1ji1y-2VlDme1Qta_qAv0TSGWXVsriTCT2d-IURm3LhsNlV0vju7qbG5VCcEU5Etw8BMlsw_qD9BbgMr1v278cwMpxYl9L83xymlWCOrfpFAPEfQJToXRCRF_vLtWq9uqfOyP9smq512-g/4vc/6CVqspjmSbOnEYgGHKRp-g/h1/h001.bZ9VkiwSoUP3A14qVo80AFyBr4O4CeHR6-UXS9LFXmg) Keith Self built his whole career on that trick. Your Muslim neighbor. Your immigrant neighbor. Whoever keeps you scared enough to stop asking why your grocery bill went up. But for all his fearmongering, it's clear that the one thing that truly frightens Keith Self is the prospect of having to talk to an actual voter. My team and I have been out every day of early voting greeting folks at the polls across the district. And the other day, Keith Self made an appearance himself. But unlike the rest of us, he stood in the shadows at the edge of the parking lot where cars drive in - with virtually no chance he'll face an actual conversation.

subject: I can still hear his voice: “Dad, get me out.”

body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie]
August 8, 2009, is a date I will never forget.
Just days before his 19th birthday, my son Justin was out in the fields with us, doing what this family has done for over three generations—farming the Louisiana delta. A breakdown in our combine left corn spilled across the ground, and as we worked to recover it, Justin got too close. In an instant, his pant leg was caught, and the thresher pulled him in.
I can still hear his voice: “Dad, get me out.”
And there was nothing I could do.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie]
Multiple miracles occurred that day: When it initially happened he wasn’t in pain because his nerves were pinched so tightly in the machine. Nor was he bleeding because he was caught so tight in there.
It took the jaws of life to tear apart that machine and when the metal finally gave way he let out a scream that I will never forget for the rest of my life.
The paramedics quickly sprang into action and he was airlifted to Jackson, Mississippi, where Doctors fought to save his leg, but the injury and infection from all the dirt and debris were too severe. Justin lost his leg from below the knee.
That day could have broken us. Instead, it showed me what makes Louisiana strong.
Neighbors, first responders from two parishes (what we call counties in Louisiana), and a doctor who wasn’t even on duty, Dr. Ron Gregg, a farmer himself and longtime family friend — showed up because that’s what rural communities do. They take care of each other. They don’t ask if it’s their job or jurisdiction. They just show up.
Today, Justin is 35. He runs our farm. He’s built a life, with a fiancée and a family of his own. He still hunts, fishes, and works the land — just with a prosthetic leg and the same determination that carried him through that day.
But the truth is, the kind of community that saved Justin is disappearing. Rural hospitals are closing. Doctors like Dr. Gregg—who live in our communities, who know our families—are harder to find. Too many of our kids feel like they have to leave home to build a future.
And my family, who first worked this Louisiana delta soil as slaves and sharecroppers, and now as farmers who own this land, have put too much blood into this soil for us to leave and go somewhere else.
I have to take a stand and fight for our way of life and it’s why I am proud to be the Democrat running for Senate in Louisiana.
If you believe in that fight, I’m asking you to stand with me today. A Democratic win here is the first step in taking our state back from the far-right whose policies of atomization and vicious corporatism are tearing our communities apart.
And mark my words, a win is possible, Democrats just won a deep red special election here by a landslide. The blue wave will wash over Louisiana and we will flip this seat but only if we fight for it. Will you please make a contribution of $50, $20, or even just $10 to help us in our fight to restore the Louisiana that we love so dearly. Thank you. Your support means more than you know.
Jamie Davis

Peter — for the last three years, Eli Crane has _failed_ to show up for rural Arizona.

When Arizonans needed him the most during a water crisis, he didn’t even care to be at the table in water discussions with our local leaders.

Hi there, it's Michele Tafoya!

If I were to take a guess, there's a 50/50 chance you may recognize me from a stadium's big screen.
If that's not the case, I get it... Let me at least tell you briefly about who I am and what I'm about anyway!

I should clarify first, no, I didn't make my career running for touchdowns or kicking game-winning field goals.

I worked as a sideline reporter in professional football for nearly three decades. Working in the sport for that long was a dream come true, and I wouldn't have wanted it any other way.
[Believe me, I know plenty of people who called me crazy for walking away from a career I loved. But life is short, and I was not willing to sit on the sidelines while everything I care about was on the line.](http://links.ourdefenseofamerica.com/u/click?_t=aa3ef0db03454a26b650c9ca7e919386&_m=cd326a13d6bf47438571f41c955ebe2c&_e=i8EpYQanOpTXnMEvGJZT7skxgs4BLyxG1hgcs_tsXXoQxgo_EyAhKhiExGv9QYn5QFgYfZn4x_LxUmt7K_lIHb1hVJjDMXzDf16TEK3pXbAmLiOtrMi-S7QNm10beQadcnrDxgF2iUWALRTQXIys2crs3_-pomTQrx5ScZpfLEyaTrvU5JRmlfiKWT5EcFg6vPD1UYeTOlz5L1HISDCbRUz6IwERmS396Y1x7lL-u16aQH3yVmR6-l-FF6kcwh9oksuqwbu0v08KyF8gf3VSkSmoYf6FZqQKRC06PW56hhVkc9TrsqIh6HCo0KFPMc8ed05wbvtQoQTG3vscBnD4z5cX5vsiZxZPR8gKhT2TacQGYZqwyQC9ieM6QycGwaSxqBkZVdp6W_-6IaN0VR5ofkEErUaTMGksFPOXDs4ur7Ox3DM7-q7fpYAfoya5I9mRjelGkz9jWgEflsD7Oqf2z2lQHIi5k4HnZ2hSR1DeNNWjoLFEDQl-ReRD_qi_0NnZxvHDchyuY1N8Apx4VTCOzd4aRzPC3cGiwK3PRm37S7DtRGBSNDIRk1WAqWctOhc4jq67jecTIzHm038S7ejCrNGBcGeGbWJ899i2iMoBDqlt9xilfpjUkb03LX2kzAut0Zj_kksSYa6EQB2EvzpyHlRiMy5TXGO6x4tafBlv47LnxjgIbkAwrafFPIElv_B9Kn6bHph7tEh5CKjExn-pCK9jutoL0DfkF6yo4KKTXx8iKSDcTSm63NdfkignfyiAm15HSjZgCgoy6vHZPf_gQj521yi1HDfSA_Uw4r2Mbv_vqnRuCfYVkgLh4r88aZR4loxaPyXXCrZc2mFU18MEa9McfVBa6K2zknpkpVO4ubVFDiHYQJU2W1BUwAC2xZcGuLSHfHzz1uQ35MJrMh8wx8ZPVTp6sXAr1Q_7CHXahdK8t-pgnTnjCGLIZ6S1xtvn-Y4FJKiUlSmilbbnbajjB4AhZCN8XUuvZ6E2RfA1n18Ae3xe-SwDLixrboayweqQ)
I told myself before I officially launched my race for U.S. Senate that we had to be all in or not do it at all.

I burned the boats, Patriot, and there's absolutely no looking back.
I will not be canceled. I will not apologize for values that are wholesome and good. And if my voice gives someone else the courage to use theirs, that is exactly why I did it.

I want my daughter and every young American to know one thing:
You earn your place. You think for yourself. And you never let anyone put you in a box. That's the Minnesota I'm fighting for.
Parents who speak up are called transphobes.Girls who lose opportunities are told to be quiet.And women's groups are nowhere to be found.
This is not complicated.
Girls' sports are for girls, and boys' sports are for boys.

The radical Left has done everything in its power to infiltrate some of the most vulnerable minds in our society. I launched this run because just like you, I'm sick of the indoctrination and want to bring back sanity to our country.

It's going to be FAR from easy. Minnesota hasn't had a Republican Senator in nearly two decades! However, it's ripe for a flip....with the disastrous leadership of Governor Walz and the Democratic Party in the state, people are fed up.

It's going to take a grassroots army of patriots, just like you, to propel this movement of ours to victory and shock the world.

clean_body: I walked away from EVERYTHING for this: | Hi there, it's Michele Tafoya! If I were to take a guess, there's a 50/50 chance you may recognize me from a stadium's big screen. If that's not the case, I get it... Let me at least tell you briefly about who I am and what I'm about anyway! I should clarify first, no, I didn't make my career running for touchdowns or kicking game-winning field goals. I worked as a sideline reporter in professional football for nearly three decades. Working in the sport for that long was a dream come true, and I wouldn't have wanted it any other way. I told myself before I officially launched my race for U.S. Senate that we had to be all in or not do it at all. I burned the boats, Patriot, and there's absolutely no looking back. I will not be canceled. I will not apologize for values that are wholesome and good. And if my voice gives someone else the courage to use theirs, that is exactly why I did it. I want my daughter and every young American to know one thing: You earn your place. You think for yourself. And you never let anyone put you in a box. That's the Minnesota I'm fighting for. Parents who speak up are called transphobes.Girls who lose opportunities are told to be quiet.And women's groups are nowhere to be found. This is not complicated. Girls' sports are for girls, and boys' sports are for boys. The radical Left has done everything in its power to infiltrate some of the most vulnerable minds in our society. I launched this run because just like you, I'm sick of the indoctrination and want to bring back sanity to our country. It's going to be FAR from easy. Minnesota hasn't had a Republican Senator in nearly two decades! This is going to be the most expensive and competitive battleground district in the country. There is a clear path to victory here – _if_ we are able to keep our foot on the gas for the next three days. Republicans have spent over $30 million here. A huge chunk of that has come in just the last few days. It’s an absurd amount of money. The only way we’re going to be able to fight back against this type of dark money is with your help. This is a grassroots campaign. A real sizable portion of our budget comes from people donating $1, $10 or $20 to emails like this one. We can beat Mike Lawler and take back the House for Democrats. But the only way we’ll be able to do that is if we hit our fundraising goals. With less than 72 hours to mobilize the coalition we need to win, hitting those goals has never been more important. $1 may not sound like a lot. But as you’re reading this, other neighbors and supporters have already chipped in to help finish the job in NY-17. They’re hoping you’ll do the same. name: Beto O'Rourke
subject: Why I started Powered by People:
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Powered by People, [poweredxpeople
body:
# [](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/43706?t=1&akid=241160%2E444211%2EYfcgkQ)
As a candidate who’d run big Texas campaigns, I learned that there’s important work that candidates and campaigns won’t be able to do by themselves. That’s why I started Powered by People.
While the candidates spend their time and money introducing themselves, defining their opponents, and working to persuade and inspire the electorate, our focus is registering and turning out the young Texans who have the power to decide the outcome of the elections.
We started with a registration-only model, but it didn’t have the impact we’d hoped for. We were getting young people registered, but they weren’t voting in the numbers we needed to make a difference. We learned that in a state that makes it harder than any other for young people to vote, we had to try harder to help them.
That forced us to change our model so that in addition to registering young people, our volunteers also personally stayed in touch with them over the duration of the election, to answer their questions, ensure they had what they needed to vote (proper ID, correct polling site, etc) and to personally encourage them throughout the Early Voting period until we could confirm their ballot had been cast. We never shared their contact information with a campaign, a candidate or a political party, it was always volunteers communicating directly with the voters they’d met in person.
We implemented this new approach in 2024, and at the end of the day the more than 28,000 young voters in our network turned out at a rate of 79%, compared to the 39% statewide average for the same demographic.
From that point on, we knew this worked. What we didn’t know is if it could scale big enough to make a difference.
So over the course of this year we’ve been growing this as big as we can get it. Recruiting more volunteers, setting up on more college campuses, expanding our reach to big concerts (thank you Kacey Musgraves!), clubs, coffee shops, anywhere we could find new and young potential voters.
_Kacey Musgraves' concert!_

_Prairie View A &M_
Our more than 2,000 active volunteers have personally met, helped register (or confirm registration) and then stayed in touch with more than 110,000 young Texans across the state. To be clear, we didn’t find them online, recruit them at a distance or treat them as part of a transaction. These are people that we met in person, listened to, had conversations with, high-fived after we completed their registration and have been personally staying in touch with throughout this election to make sure they vote.
As early voting has concluded, the numbers we have so far show that 55.76% of the voters in our network have voted, compared to 38.92% of all registered Texans who’ve voted so far. All of this personal contact — which takes thousands of volunteers, hundreds of thousands of hours and lots of patience and persistence — really pays off.
I’m proud of our team, our volunteers and our voters. They’re doing everything they can to help James, Gina and the ticket get across the line.
In these final days this team is reaching out to every last voter who hasn’t yet voted, personally calling and texting until we’ve done everything humanly possible to help them vote.
We can’t predict what will happen on November 3rd, but we know that the work that our volunteers and voters have done will be a significant contribution to the outcome.
I, and the whole team at Powered by People, are grateful for your support in this as we push through to the very end.
-Beto

Derek,

As an Air Force veteran, I was taught that true leadership isn’t about standing in the spotlight – it’s about lifting up the team around you.
Over the past few months, I’ve traveled across Pennsylvania and around the country to campaign alongside dedicated Democrats running in critical battleground districts. I’ve also worked hard to channel vital resources directly into these tight races to make sure our candidates have the tools they need to win.
I wanted to share this update with you directly, because every mile traveled and every candidate supported was made possible by you.
Whether you chipped in $5 or $50, your investment extended far beyond our district. You helped build momentum nationwide. Every door knocked and every ad run in these key seats has a piece of your generosity in it, and I want to make sure you take credit for that shared success.
We are right on the verge of retaking the House majority – and that is cause for real hope. But if my service taught me anything, it’s that you never declare victory until the mission is finished. We cannot afford to be overconfident or slow down now.
**[If you’re in a position to help us finish strong, would you consider chipping in $5 or whatever works for you today?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142633557/657537588/685235109?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk1327-fr-nd&recurring=0&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDIvMS82NDkxMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhNTc3NDZhOS02NWQ1LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=mWriQ9NbwxhrG3FS9ClmANawOzQzAYNtm5tvieMZTRw=)**
Thank you for your trust, your partnership, and your commitment to doing the work together.
There’s work to be done,
Chrissy Houlahan

I can’t help but make a Halloween connection to some of the election-related headlines floating around right now.
Republican candidates have dressed themselves up in some very unconvincing costumes — pretending to not have extreme anti-democracy views and pretending to not be radicals who are intent on continuing to rip away our freedoms. But let’s face it: they’re not winning any costume contests.
And you might say that Republicans are running the “Trick AND Treat” playbook:
First, they try all the dirty tricks — like manipulating maps and making it harder to vote.
Then, when that’s not enough to guarantee their victory, they resort to basically going door to door begging for treats from the wealthiest, most powerful people in the country. And that begging is getting results:
The New York Times:“Billionaire Republicans are vastly outspending Democrats...This election will be the most expensive in history”
The Washington Post:“Musk breaks donor record as the ultrarich pour $2.7 billion into the midterms...the other largest donors this cycle lean heavily Republican”
It’s not a coincidence that major right-wing donors are targeting states like Ohio, Georgia, Texas, and Florida, where some of the most important governors’ races are up for grabs.
[This is now the most expensive — and most important — election of our lifetimes. And tonight’s our final monthly fundraising deadline before voting ends. We don’t need to match the big money on the other side, but we can’t get drowned out, especially among a few endorsed candidates who need one final boost before Tuesday. And we really need one last push from grassroots donors like you to support Democracy Defenders running in tight races — these are elections that are critical to how democracy functions in key states. = | If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: = | = = | = = | = I can’t help but make a Halloween connection to some of the election-related headlines floating around right now. Republican candidates have dressed themselves up in some very unconvincing costumes — pretending to not have extreme anti-democracy views and pretending to not be radicals who are intent on continuing to rip away our freedoms. But let’s face it: they’re not winning any costume contests. And you might say that Republicans are running the “Trick AND Treat” playbook: First, they try all the dirty tricks — like manipulating maps and making it harder to vote. Then, when that’s not enough to guarantee their victory, they resort to basically going door to door begging for treats from the wealthiest, most powerful people in the country. And that begging is getting results: The New York Times:“Billionaire Republicans are vastly outspending Democrats...This election will be the most expensive in history” The Washington Post:“Musk breaks donor record as the ultrarich pour $2.7 billion into the midterms...the other largest donors this cycle lean heavily Republican” It’s not a coincidence that major right-wing donors are targeting states like Ohio, Georgia, Texas, and Florida, where some of the most important governors’ races are up for grabs. = Thank you, Claire Low Director of Political and Campaigns National Democratic Redistricting Committee = = | | Paid for by the National Democratic Redistricting Committee, John Bisognano, President. | | | | | | | ---|---|---|---|---|---|--- National Democratic Redistricting Committee 712 H St NE, #25 Washington, DC 20002 United States if you'd like to receive fewer emails from the NDRC. To set up your profile and discover more on Substack, [click here](https://substack.com/redirect/3353568a-be25-442c-934b-0ed28fa79846?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Sherrod here. I wish I had better news today, but you deserve to know.
We only brought in half of the revenue we were expecting from Google and Facebook at the end of the week. I can't overstate this: _that is not good news for our campaign._
It looks like everything was running as it should, so we're digging in to see what may be going on. Here's what we know for sure: we have a major budget gap at the same time we need to be ramping up our final GOTV efforts.
Asking for money is my least favorite part of running for Senate, but that's what I need to do. If we can't make up for our slowdown, we will run out of resources tonight. Our bank account is almost at $0.
Early voting ends in Ohio tomorrow. I need your help so we can continue sharing our message. **[If you can afford to make a contribution to help us make up for this deficit, it will have an immediate impact.](https://substack.com/redirect/18d82be2-3252-4b41-9ca8-ca068218d803?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** We're so close to the finish line. Thanks for stepping up.
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/18d82be2-3252-4b41-9ca8-ca068218d803?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
[I've written to you about our Google and Facebook ads before](https://substack.com/redirect/66c38759-56ce-4d66-88dd-079305af3ad9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). They aren't necessarily the most glamorous part of our operation, but they really matter.
For one, these ads allow us to reach undecided voters and adjust our targeting much more quickly than we can with our field operation or TV ads. So many voters use these platforms - and it's important for us to have a plan to reach them where they are.
You might also be surprised to hear that our Google and Facebook ads account for 25% of our total online fundraising every week. We have a massive digital outreach program, and they're one of the best ways we can mobilize supporters and ensure folks can easily engage with our campaign.
The issue is, our online fundraising from these ads hit a wall on Thursday and Friday. We're not sure why. It looks like our ads are running properly. But we do know that if this trend continues, we'll be out of money a lot sooner than we expected - as soon as tonight.
Look, asking for money is my least favorite part of this. I'd much rather be talking to folks in person, sharing a coffee with you, hearing about your stories. But if we can't make up for this setback, our campaign won't be able to operate through Election Day.

Dear
Peter,
This past week, I had the pleasure of joining guest host Sam Peters on The Wayne Allyn Root show to discuss my campaign for Assembly District 37.

We covered a lot of ground during the interview, including the coming fight over tax increases, the Democrats’ dangerous attacks on our brave men and women in law enforcement and how they’re undermining our public safety, and the importance of rebuilding Nevada’s economy in a way that promotes economic liberty and prosperity.

Above all, we talked about what’s at stake this November — the competing visions between myself and my left-wing opponent, and why winning this race is so important to breaking the Democrats’ stranglehold on our state legislature.

I hope you’ll click below to take a listen ... and as always, I’d love any feedback or comments you’d like to provide!
https://andyfornevada.com/andy-matthews_sam-peters_8-28-20/
***

By the way, I was also honored this week to receive the endorsement of the National Rifle Association. I’ve long been a proud champion of the Second Amendment, and it’s an absolute thrill to have the support of our nation’s preeminent defender of the right to bear arms.

Especially today, with Nevada’s Democrats waging a relentless assault on our Second Amendment rights (for her part, my opponent received an “F” grade from the NRA), it’s more important than ever that we elect those who will unapologetically defend our Constitution. And you can count on me to do exactly that in Carson City.

For Nevada’s future,

Andy

Across the country, voters are increasingly expressing frustration with Republicans in Washington — especially when it comes to the cost of living and the economy — and recent national polling has shown growing support for Democrats heading into November. clean_body: It's time to take care of business. | = Peter, It's Gretchen Whitmer. I know we're all concerned with the chaos coming out of Washington, D.C. We're seeing healthcare and basic necessities being ripped away from the people who need it most and dangerous attempts to roll back our fundamental freedoms. But the political environment is changing. Across the country, voters are increasingly expressing frustration with Republicans in Washington — especially when it comes to the cost of living and the economy — and recent national polling has shown growing support for Democrats heading into November. That shift follows powerful Democratic victories already in 2025 and 2026, including races where reproductive freedom and fundamental rights have been front and center. It's time to take care of business, Peter — which, in Democratic politics, means one thing: It's time to look to EMILYs List. My friends at EMILYs List have been helping Democratic pro-choice women win elections for 40 years and counting. Their role in changing the face of power in American politics can't be overstated, and I'm proud to be an EMILYs List woman myself. = | = Here's what I know for sure: More freedom is better than less. Some rights, like the right to make our own damn decisions about our own damn bodies, are nonnegotiable. And when more women are at the decision-making table, we all do better. I'm thrilled that in 2026, a record 10 Democratic women governors now hold office — every single one of them an EMILYs List woman. I'm here to tell you firsthand, Peter: We need more women in charge of our states. Republicans haven't taken a day off from coming after our fundamental freedoms, and with Election Day just a few days away, they're throwing everything they've got at our women candidates. We can't take a day off either. This is the last end-of-month deadline before the election, and what EMILYs List raises tonight will help Democratic pro-choice women finish strong on Tuesday. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue, your donation will go through immediately: = | = ---|--- = | = = | = Thanks for stepping up, Gretchen = Gov. Patriot,

Most of what we send you is strategy: states, numbers, the plan to win. This one is about why we do this work at all. And that starts with Charlie Kirk.

Charlie launched Turning Point in the shadows of the Obama re-election campaign headquarters in Chicago. He was 18 years old.

Every established political force on the Left and the Right tried to stop him.

They failed.

What Charlie started grew into what is **the most influential activist organization in modern American history**.

We were privileged to work with him and be a part of this movement.

We joined Charlie because we believed our mission was the only viable way to save this country. Charlie was willing to do what nobody else in the conservative movement would do. He went looking for young Americans who cared enough about this country to act, and he gave them a reason to fight.

Then came 2020...

Under President Biden, we saw corruption, weaponization of the government, and a government promoting values that put Americans last.

Charlie was adamant that we do everything we could possibly do to fix this in 2024. **We DID IT** , and we must continue for 2026 and 2028 to have a shot at saving this country.

Now, it is on us to continue Charlie's vision and mission.

Every single day, we work to continue his legacy of recruiting, training, and mobilizing a new generation of citizens who love this country enough to do something about it.

That work does not stop at the campus gates. It's now changing the direction of the nation.

Right now, ballot chasers supported by Turning Point PAC are in the field in **states that will determine not just 2026, but the 2028 Presidential election**.

They are meeting voters face to face. They are building real relationships in these communities. They are chasing every ballot, whether it's cast on Election Day or by mail.

This is how we build the Red Wall.

With more and more attention (and resources) focused on the Kansas Senate race, we're asking you to **[chip in a donation to Adam Hamilton's grassroots campaign](https://substack.com/redirect/f1531bdf-1296-4084-98e3-b350a6e563b6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** before the election. Keep reading for the latest updates from Adam.
Friends,
With early voting underway in Kansas and Election Day just days away, Roger Marshall is _panicking_. After all, Roll Call named him one of the most vulnerable senators in the country and _multiple_ election experts have switched this race from a safe seat to a toss-up.
And you know what? He should be anxious. After turning his back on Kansans and consistently voting to make their lives harder and more expensive, people are fed up. They're ready for a leader who will listen to them and work to solve their problems, not be a yes-man to a party and an administration that doesn't put hardworking Kansas families first.
But Sen. Marshall has what he's hoping is an ace up his sleeve: **President Trump is returning to tomorrow to hold another rally supporting Marshall.**
The president coming here again so close to Election Day is proof that Washington insiders are worried. _They know people are fed up, they know our grassroots movement is surging and they know we have what it takes to win._
**But folks, I 'm worried too.** When the president rallies for someone, big money often follows. Top GOP super PACs have already spent nearly $40 million on this race, and after Sunday, they're almost certainly going to pour _even more_ resources into defeating us.
**They 're pulling out all the stops because they know that, unlike me, Roger Marshall is a yes-man for party bosses. He's spent a decade in Washington rubber-stamping the policies his party has told him to support, even when those policies hurt the people he was elected to represent. **
In the past year alone, he's voted to slash the healthcare assistance that thousands of Kansans rely on, supported Medicaid cuts that have put 28 rural hospitals at risk of closing, backed a war that's driven diesel prices to record highs and signed off on the tariffs that cost Kansans hundreds of dollars every month.
**Now, the establishment is going all out to save this seat for him so he can keep putting Washington insiders over Kansans.**
Look, the reality is that we have what it takes to retire Roger Marshall. If we didn't, the president wouldn't be coming back to try and rescue him. But that doesn't change the fact that Marshall and his allies continue to outspend us at an alarming rate. They're blanketing the airwaves with attack ads against me -- and if we can't find a way to keep up, we may lose the chance to defeat Marshall and flip this seat.
I know Kansans are ready for change. I know their enthusiasm for better leadership -- leadership that actually fights for _them_ -- is surging. But if we can't keep ads on the air and fund our get-out-the-vote efforts, we'll lose ground in this critical moment ... and we won't have time to make it up.
**My team and I have set an ambitious final end-of-month goal to raise $3 million to help us meet this moment. That 's what it will take to respond to the escalated attacks that are coming. So, I'm personally asking: [Will you chip in whatever you can right now to our campaign to help us reach our final end-of-month goal, get our message out there to every Kansan and flip this seat?](https://substack.com/redirect/f1531bdf-1296-4084-98e3-b350a6e563b6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
They're scared they're going to lose their yes-man. With your help, we can prove them right.
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/f1531bdf-1296-4084-98e3-b350a6e563b6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Thanks for all you do,
Adam Hamilton

They're ready for a leader who will listen to them and work to solve their problems, not be a yes-man to a party and an administration that doesn't put hardworking Kansas families first. But Sen. Marshall has what he's hoping is an ace up his sleeve: President Trump is returning to tomorrow to hold another rally supporting Marshall. The president coming here again so close to Election Day is proof that Washington insiders are worried. They know people are fed up, they know our grassroots movement is surging and they know we have what it takes to win. But folks, I 'm worried too. When the president rallies for someone, big money often follows. Top GOP super PACs have already spent nearly $40 million on this race, and after Sunday, they're almost certainly going to pour even more resources into defeating us. They 're pulling out all the stops because they know that, unlike me, Roger Marshall is a yes-man for party bosses. He's spent a decade in Washington rubber-stamping the policies his party has told him to support, even when those policies hurt the people he was elected to represent. In the past year alone, he's voted to slash the healthcare assistance that thousands of Kansans rely on, supported Medicaid cuts that have put 28 rural hospitals at risk of closing, backed a war that's driven diesel prices to record highs and signed off on the tariffs that cost Kansans hundreds of dollars every month. Now, the establishment is going all out to save this seat for him so he can keep putting Washington insiders over Kansans. Look, the reality is that we have what it takes to retire Roger Marshall. If we didn't, the president wouldn't be coming back to try and rescue him. But that doesn't change the fact that Marshall and his allies continue to outspend us at an alarming rate. They're blanketing the airwaves with attack ads against me -- and if we can't find a way to keep up, we may lose the chance to defeat Marshall and flip this seat. I know Kansans are ready for change. I know their enthusiasm for better leadership -- leadership that actually fights for them -- is surging. But if we can't keep ads on the air and fund our get-out-the-vote efforts, we'll lose ground in this critical moment ... and we won't have time to make it up. My team and I have set an ambitious final end-of-month goal to raise $3 million to help us meet this moment. That 's what it will take to respond to the escalated attacks that are coming. So, I'm personally asking: They're scared they're going to lose their yes-man. With your help, we can prove them right. Thanks for all you do, Adam Hamilton | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Adam Hamilton for Kansas 548 Market Street PMB 72296, San Francisco, CA 94104 ? ?
